checklist.title: Conditions to check (not a decision)
checklist.involuntary: Your unemployment is involuntary, for example a dismissal or the end of a fixed-term contract.
checklist.contributions: You have at least 360 days of registered pay in the 24 months before you became unemployed.
checklist.registration: You are registered at the employment centre (IEFP).
checklist.ready: You live in Portugal and are able and available to work.
checklist.deadline: You request the benefit within 90 days of becoming unemployed.
checklist.note: Only Segurança Social decides whether you are entitled. This list is a reminder, not a verdict.

guide.example: Someone aged {{age}}, earning {{gross}} a month in 14 payments, with {{months}} months and {{years}} years of registered pay in the last 20, living alone. The reference pay is {{reference}} a day, so 65% for 30 days gives {{monthly}} a month ({{daily}} a day). The period is {{base}} days plus {{extra}} extra days, {{days}} days in total, so about {{total}} over the whole period. Compared with an estimated net pay of {{net}} a month, the income drop is {{drop}} a month.
guide.methodReference: The reference remuneration (RR) is all pay registered in the oldest 12 of the 14 months before the month you became unemployed, including the holiday and Christmas allowances, divided by 360. The calculator takes 14 or 12 times your monthly salary.
guide.methodAmount: The daily benefit is 65% of the RR. The monthly figure is 30 days of it.
guide.methodLimits: The monthly benefit cannot exceed 2.5 times the IAS ({{max}} in 2026) or 75% of the net RR, and cannot be below 1 IAS ({{ias}}), except when the net RR is lower than the IAS. The 1 IAS minimum prevails over the 75% cap, but the benefit never exceeds the net RR itself (art. 29 of Decreto-Lei n.º 220/2006). When the pay used is at least the minimum wage ({{rmmg}}), the minimum is 1.15 IAS.
guide.methodNet: The net RR is the RR minus 11% Social Security and the IRS withholding rate (art. 29 n.º 4 of Decreto-Lei n.º 220/2006). The rate comes from the withholding tables for your household, according to the net RR. The calculator looks up the 2026 mainland tables at the RR minus 11% and applies that rate to the whole RR, as a single holder, or as married with two earners if your partner is in the household.
guide.methodIncrease: The benefit goes up 10% when both partners are unemployed and registered, or you are the only parent, and there are children or dependants. It must be requested. The calculator applies it to the limited amount and never above 2.5 IAS.
guide.methodDuration: The duration depends on your age and months with registered pay, plus extra days for every full 5 years with registered pay in the last 20: 30 days up to age 39, 45 days from 40 to 49 and 60 days from 50.
guide.methodNoReduction: The old 10% cut after 180 days of payment is not applied: the 2026 Segurança Social guide does not list it.
guide.methodTax: The Segurança Social guide says the benefit does not have to be declared for IRS. Confirm your own case with the Tax Authority.
guide.methodBudget: The monthly benefit is the income to plan with. Compare it with your net pay to see the drop, then see how long your savings cover the gap.
guide.unsupportedTransitional: The transitional table for people who already met the contribution requirement on 31 March 2012 and have not been unemployed since. The calculator uses only the general table.
guide.unsupportedSocial: The social unemployment benefit (subsídio social de desemprego), which the guide says can only be requested until 30 December 2026.
guide.unsupportedSelfEmployed: Self-employed workers, company managers, partial unemployment benefit, teachers with their own contribution rules and former invalidity pensioners.
guide.unsupportedOther: Pay that varied a lot in the 12 months counted, periods without registered pay inside them, other income and the one-off lump-sum payment to start a business.
guide.sourceGuide: Segurança Social: Guia Prático Subsídio de Desemprego (v4.79, 16 October 2026), which also lists the 2026 IAS of 537.13 euros (Portaria n.º 480-A/2025/1) and the minimum wage of 920 euros (Decreto-Lei n.º 139/2025)
guide.sourceLaw: Decreto-Lei n.º 220/2006, as amended: the unemployment protection regime
guide.sourceIncrease: Decreto-Lei n.º 119/2021: the 10% increase for households with children and the 1.15 IAS minimum
guide.reviewed: Rules and 2026 values reviewed on 19 November 2026 against the Segurança Social guide (v. October 2026), the gov.pt service page for the benefit (updated 19 October 2026) and the text of art. 29 of Decreto-Lei n.º 220/2006 (read in a secondary copy, not in the official consolidated version). The order of the limits follows that article; the order of the 10% increase relative to the limits is not stated in the sources we read, so it is our simplification. The gov.pt page works one example with a 9.4% IRS rate that we cannot reproduce from the 2026 tables, so the real cap can be lower than shown. The end of the 10% cut after 180 days is taken from the guide and press reports, not from the consolidated law.

fields.dependants: Children up to 16 (or 24 with child benefit)

allowanceOptions.twelfths: In twelfths (the salary already includes them)

help.gross: The base salary in the months counted, before Social Security and IRS. Holiday and Christmas allowances are not part of the reference pay.
help.allowances: In twelfths, the calculator takes out the two allowances to get the base salary the reference pay uses.
help.sickDays: Total days on the sick note (CIT), counted from the first day. Employees can receive up to 1,095 days.
help.dependants: Used for the 5-point increase, which applies with 3 or more children, with the disability bonus, or when the reference pay is 500 euros a month or less.
help.disabilityBonus: The bonificação por deficiência, paid with child benefit (abono de família) for a descendant with a disability. It also gives the 5-point increase, whatever the reference pay.

result.total: Estimated total paid by Segurança Social
result.waiting: Waiting days (not paid by Segurança Social)
result.firstGap: Income gap in the first 30 days
result.averageGap: Average monthly income gap over the whole leave
result.increaseApplied: The 5-point increase (reference pay of 500 euros or less, 3 or more children, or the disability bonus) is included.
result.allWaiting: Every day of this leave is a waiting day, so Segurança Social pays nothing. Check whether your contract or collective agreement makes your employer pay these days.
result.waitingNote: Segurança Social does not pay the first 3 days. Whether your employer pays them depends on your contract or collective agreement.
result.estimate: An estimate for planning, not a decision. Segurança Social calculates the real amount from your registered pay.

limit.none: The daily amount is the percentage of your reference pay for each band; no limit applied.
limit.minimum: The daily amount was raised to the minimum of {{min}} (30% of the minimum wage).
limit.referencePay: Your reference pay is below {{min}} a day, so the benefit equals the reference pay.
limit.netCap: The daily amount was limited to the estimated net value of your reference pay.

checklist.title: Conditions to check (not a decision)
checklist.certificate: You have a sick note (CIT) from a doctor, sent electronically to Segurança Social.
checklist.guarantee: You have 6 months of registered pay (they do not have to be consecutive) on the day you stop working.
checklist.professionalIndex: You worked at least 12 days in the first four of the last six months, counting the month you stop.
checklist.waiting: There is no waiting period for a hospital stay or outpatient surgery, tuberculosis, or an illness that starts during parental benefit and goes beyond it. The calculator only has a switch for the first.
checklist.note: Only Segurança Social decides whether you are entitled. This list is a reminder, not a verdict.

guide.example: An employee earning {{gross}} a month in 14 payments, on sick leave for {{days}} days with no hospital stay. The reference pay is {{reference}} a day. Days 1 to 3 are waiting days, so the first band pays 27 days at 55% and the next 15 days at 60%: {{total}} in total. Normal net pay is {{net}} a month; over the leave the average shortfall is {{gap}} a month.
guide.methodReference: The reference pay (RR) is the pay registered in the 6 oldest of the 8 months before the month the sick leave starts, without holiday and Christmas allowances, divided by 180. The calculator uses your monthly salary divided by 30.
guide.methodBands: The daily benefit is a percentage of the RR that grows with the length of the leave: 55% up to 30 days, 60% from day 31 to 90, 70% from day 91 to 365 and 75% beyond that, up to 1,095 days for employees. The days count from the first day of the leave, waiting days included.
guide.methodWaiting: Employees have a waiting period of 3 days that Segurança Social does not pay. With a hospital stay or outpatient surgery, tuberculosis, or an illness that starts during parental benefit and goes beyond it, payment starts on day 1.
guide.methodMinimum: The daily benefit cannot be below {{min}} (30% of the {{rmmg}} minimum wage). If the RR itself is lower, the benefit equals the RR.
guide.methodIncrease: At 55% and 60%, the percentage goes up 5 points when any one of these applies (art. 17(1) of Decree-Law 28/2004): the RR is at most 500 euros a month, the household has 3 or more children up to 16 (or 24 with child benefit), or the household has children who receive the disability bonus on child benefit. The conditions are alternatives, and the 5 points are added once even when more than one applies (art. 17(3)). The calculator asks about all three.
guide.methodNetCap: The daily benefit also cannot exceed the net value of the RR. The calculator estimates it with 11% Social Security and the 2026 mainland IRS withholding rate for a single holder.
guide.methodGap: The income gap compares your normal net pay (14 or 12 payments averaged over 12 months) with what Segurança Social pays. Holiday and Christmas allowances are not recreated for the days on leave.
guide.methodBudget: The gap is the income you have to cover from savings or by cutting spending while you are on leave. Use it to size your cushion.
guide.unsupportedTuberculosis: Tuberculosis, paid at 80% or 100% of the RR depending on dependants, with no time limit.
guide.unsupportedSelfEmployed: Self-employed workers (10 days of waiting, up to 365 days), voluntary social insurance and domestic workers.
guide.unsupportedShort: Short absences covered by the SNS 24 self-declaration of illness: we did not model their rules.
guide.unsupportedOther: Fewer than 6 months of registered pay, pay that varied a lot, compensation for work accidents or occupational disease, and collective agreements that top up the benefit.
guide.sourceGuide: Segurança Social: Guia Prático Subsídio de Doença (ISS 5001, v4.55, 23 October 2026), with the 2026 minimum wage of 920 euros
guide.sourceLaw: Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2004, consolidated version in the Diário da República: the sickness protection regime (art. 17 in the wording of art. 9 of Decreto-Lei n.º 133/2012, with the disability bonus condition in art. 17(1)(c))
guide.reviewed: Rules and 2026 values reviewed on 20 November 2026 against the Segurança Social guide and the consolidated text of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2004 in the Diário da República. The three alternative conditions for the 5-point increase and the floor above 500 euros come from art. 17. Art. 17(4) says the 500 euro figure is updated with the IAS, but we found no act that publishes an updated figure, and the guide in force (ISS 5001 v4.55, 23 October 2026) still gives 500,00 euros, so we keep 500. The estimate of net pay behind the net cap is our simplification.
guide.methodFloor: Above a reference pay of 500 euros a month, the daily benefit at 55% and 60% cannot be lower than the increased benefit computed on 500 euros: 60% and 65% of 500 divided by 30, which is {{floor55}} and {{floor60}} a day (art. 17(2) of Decree-Law 28/2004). It only matters for a reference pay a little above 500 euros, up to about 545 euros, when no increase applies. It does not apply to the 70% and 75% bands.

guide.example: A diesel car with a {{cc}} cm³ engine, official WLTP emissions of {{co2}} g/km and first registered in {{year}} owes {{tax}} of IUC a year. Setting aside {{monthly}} a month covers it.
guide.methodAdditional: Category B cars first registered after 1 January 2017 pay an additional rate when emissions are high: €31.77 above 205 g/km (WLTP) or 180 g/km (NEDC), and €63.74 above 260 g/km (WLTP) or 250 g/km (NEDC). The additional rate is also multiplied by the coefficient. The legal text does not limit it by fuel, so the calculator applies it to every fuel.
guide.methodDiesel: Diesel cars also pay the diesel surcharge (adicional de IUC, article 216 of Lei n.º 82-B/2014, kept in force for 2026 by the State Budget). It depends on engine size, applies to categories A and B, and is added after the coefficient, not multiplied by it.
guide.methodPayment: Until 2026 the IUC is paid in the month of the registration anniversary. Decreto-Lei n.º 161/2026 (4 August 2026) moves it to one yearly assessment per taxpayer, covering all vehicles. 2027 is a transitional year: one payment in October up to €500, otherwise two in July and October (or all in July). From 2028 it is settled by April and paid in April up to €100, in April and October from €100 up to €500, and in April, July and October above €500. The thresholds apply to the total for all your vehicles.
guide.methodBudget: The monthly provision divides the annual amount by 12, so the money is ready when the bill arrives.
guide.exemption: Fully electric cars in category B are exempt from IUC, and the calculator shows zero. Plug-in hybrids and other vehicles are taxed by their engine size and CO2 as shown on the registration document, so enter those values.
guide.assumptionYear: The rates are the {{taxYear}} tables of the Código do IUC (articles 9 and 10), in the wording of {{law}}. The Portal das Finanças lists no later change to these rates.
guide.assumptionPayment: The 2026 due month follows the registration anniversary rule, which the explanatory preamble of Decreto-Lei n.º 161/2026 confirms is the rule in force today. From 2027 the tax is assessed per taxpayer across all their vehicles: add each of your cars, and enter the IUC of any other vehicles as other IUC, so the instalment months follow your total (the law applies its thresholds to that total). The schedules for 2027 and 2028 give each month's amount for the cars you added; with one car, its share of each instalment. In the year of registration the tax is paid within 30 days of the registration deadline.
guide.assumptionEducational: This is an educational estimate, not tax advice. The amount on the notice from the Tax Authority is the one that counts.

help.dates: The coefficient applies only when the property was held for more than 24 months. The calculator covers sales in {{saleYear}}.

help.reinvested: Counts purchases from 24 months before up to 36 months after the sale, in Portugal or the EU/EEA.
help.loanRepaid: The part of the proceeds that repays the home loan of the sold property.
help.taxValue: The valor patrimonial tributário on the property's caderneta predial at the date of the sale. If it is above the price, the gain is calculated on it. Leave it empty if you don't know it.
help.purchaseValue: The value the IMT of your purchase was paid on: the price, or the VPT at the time if it was higher (art. 46(1) of the CIRS).

result.loss: The sale ended in a loss, so no gain is added to your income.
result.zero: There is no gain, so there is no extra IRS.
result.cashAfter: Proceeds left after selling costs, loan repaid and estimated IRS
result.realizationValue: Sale value used for the gain
result.taxValueApplied: The VPT is higher than the price, so the gain is calculated on it, the value the IMT of the sale is paid on (art. 44(2) of the CIRS). The proceeds left use the price you receive.

checklist.title: Conditions to check for the reinvestment exclusion
checklist.domicile: The sold home was your permanent home, with your tax domicile there, in the 12 months before the sale.
checklist.reinvest: The proceeds, net of the loan repaid, are reinvested in another permanent home, in land to build one or in works on it, in Portugal or the EU/EEA, between 24 months before and 36 months after the sale.
checklist.declare: You state the intention to reinvest, and the amount, in the IRS return for the year of the sale.
checklist.occupy: The new home becomes your permanent home, with your tax domicile there, within 12 months of the reinvestment.
checklist.register: For land or construction, the registry is requested within 48 months of the sale and the home is used as your residence until the end of the fifth year after it.
checklist.note: This list is a reminder, not a verdict. The Tax Authority decides whether the conditions are met.

guide.example: A home bought in {{purchaseYear}} for {{purchaseValue}} and sold in {{saleYear}} for {{saleValue}}. The purchase value is updated by the {{coefficient}} coefficient to {{adjustedPurchase}}, and {{expenses}} of expenses are deducted, leaving a gain of {{gain}}. Half of it, {{included}}, is added to other income of {{otherIncome}}, which adds about {{extraTax}} of IRS.
guide.methodGain: Gain = sale value minus the acquisition value updated by the coefficient, minus the acquisition and sale expenses and the works of the last 12 years (CIRS articles 44, 46, 50 and 51). The acquisition value is the value the IMT of the purchase was paid on (art. 46(1)).
guide.methodCoefficient: The currency devaluation coefficient of the year of purchase applies only if the property was held for more than 24 months. The {{saleYear}} values come from {{portaria}} and are stored for purchases from {{firstYear}}.
guide.methodExpenses: Expenses must be necessary, effectively paid and supported by documents: IMT and Imposto do Selo of the purchase, agency fees, and works of the last 12 years with invoices.
guide.methodHalf: Only 50% of a positive gain is added to the other income of the year and taxed at the progressive {{saleYear}} IRS brackets. The extra IRS shown is the tax with the gain minus the tax without it.
guide.methodExemption: A gain on your own permanent home is excluded when the proceeds, net of the loan repaid, are reinvested in another one within the legal window. If only part is reinvested, the same proportion of the gain is excluded.
guide.methodCash: The proceeds left subtract the selling costs, the loan repaid and the estimated IRS from the sale value. It does not subtract what you spend on the next home.
guide.scopeSupported: Individuals who are Portuguese tax residents selling a property held as a private asset, bought from {{firstYear}} on, in {{saleYear}}.
guide.assumptionBrackets: The extra IRS uses the {{saleYear}} annual IRS brackets on the income you enter, as an estimate of the effect on the annual return. Joint taxation is modelled as splitting the income in two.
guide.assumptionNotModelled: The calculator does not check the reinvestment conditions. The coefficients were checked against the table of {{portaria}} in the Diário da República.
guide.assumptionEducational: This is an educational estimate, not tax advice. The IRS assessment from the Tax Authority is the one that counts.
guide.sourceGains: CIRS, article 43: gains and losses (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.sourceExemption: CIRS, article 10: exclusion for reinvestment in the own permanent home (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.reviewed: Rules and coefficients for {{saleYear}} reviewed on {{reviewed}}.
guide.methodTaxValue: The sale value is the price, unless the value the IMT of the sale is paid on is higher (art. 44(2) of the CIRS). IMT is paid on the higher of the price and the VPT (art. 12(1) of the CIMT), so a VPT above the price raises the gain and the amount to reinvest for the exclusion. You can prove that the real price was lower through the procedure of art. 139 of the CIRC (art. 44(5) and (6) of the CIRS); the calculator does not model that proof.
guide.sourceRealization: CIRS, article 44: realisation value and the IMT value floor (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.sourceAcquisition: CIRS, article 46: acquisition value of a property bought for a price (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.sourceCorrection: CIRS, article 50: currency devaluation correction after 24 months (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.sourceExpenses: CIRS, article 51: works of the last 12 years and acquisition and sale expenses (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.sourceImt: CIMT, article 12: IMT is paid on the higher of the price and the VPT (consulted 20 November 2026)
guide.scopeUnsupportedBody: Non-residents, properties bought before {{firstYear}}, companies and self-employed property in a business, inheritances and gifts, homes that received public support above 30% of their tax value, the solidarity surcharge and deductions from tax.

IRS withholding is {{withholding}} and Social Security is {{socialSecurity}}, so {{net}} reaches your account.
guide.ruleAmount: The Christmas allowance equals one month's pay and is due by 15 December (Código do Trabalho, art. 263, n.º 1).
guide.ruleHiringYear: In the year you are hired, the allowance is proportional to the time worked in the calendar year (art. 263, n.º 2). The calculator counts calendar days from your start date to 31 December; some employers count months, which can differ by a few euros.
guide.methodPlan: The net figure is extra money that arrives once a year, so it works best with a plan: goals first, then the expenses it has to cover.

guide.example: You started on 15 March 2026 with a base salary of {{salary}} a month, unmarried with no dependants, in mainland Portugal. You have 9 complete months, so you earn {{days}} holiday days, and the holiday allowance is {{gross}} before deductions. IRS withholding is {{withholding}} and Social Security is {{socialSecurity}}, so {{net}} reaches your account.
guide.ruleAmount: The holiday allowance covers the minimum length of holidays, on top of your holiday pay (Código do Trabalho, art. 264, n.º 2), and is paid before the holidays start unless agreed otherwise in writing (n.º 3). For a full year it equals one month's pay.
guide.ruleHiringYear: In the year you are hired you earn 2 working days of holiday per complete month of the contract, up to 20 days (art. 239, n.º 1). The calculator scales the allowance by those days over the 22 working days of a full year, so 18 days gives 18/22 of a month's pay.
guide.methodPlan: The net figure is money meant for time off, so it helps to set it aside for the trip, with a target and a date, before it is spent.

modes.twelfths: In twelfths (added to each monthly salary)

help.gross: Your base salary before allowances, Social Security and IRS.
help.mode: A lump sum is paid in one go. In twelfths, the allowance is split over the months you work in the year and paid with each salary.

startDate.christmas: Leave empty if you worked the whole of {{year}}. In the year you start, the Christmas allowance is proportional to the time worked.
startDate.holiday: Leave empty if you were already employed before {{year}}. In the year of hiring you earn 2 working days of holiday per complete month, up to 20.

result.netTwelfth: Extra net amount in each monthly salary
result.twelfthGross: Gross twelfth added to each salary
result.holidayDays: Holiday days counted: {{days}} of 22 ({{percent}} of a full allowance).
result.noAllowanceYet: With no complete month yet in the hiring year, there is no holiday allowance to pay. The 2 working days per month only start counting once a month is complete.
result.noWithholdingOnTwelfth: Each twelfth is withheld at the effective rate of the whole allowance, which is 0% at this level, so no IRS is withheld on it. Your payroll may add the twelfth to the month's salary and withhold on the total, which withholds more.

guide.methodWithholding: Each payment is withheld on its own with the 2026 monthly table, never added to the month's salary: Despacho n.º 233-A/2026 (n.º 10) asks employers to show a separate effective rate for each remuneration, as in the months the holiday and Christmas allowances are paid.
guide.methodTwelfths: Paid in twelfths, the allowance is split evenly over the months you work in the year (12 for a whole year). Each twelfth is withheld on its own at the effective rate of the whole allowance, the usual payroll practice since Lei n.º 11/2013, art. 3 (not stated in the Despacho). Your payroll may instead add the twelfth to the month's salary and withhold on the total, which usually withholds more: check your payslip.
guide.methodSocialSecurity: Employee Social Security is 11% of the gross allowance.
guide.unsupportedNovember: The one-off adjustment for income paid in November 2026 (Despacho 12523-A/2026, mainland) is ignored. An allowance paid in November would be withheld at half.
guide.unsupportedOther: Only the base salary counts. Seniority supplements, other pay components, a contract ending or suspended during the year, collective agreements that pay more and employer costs are outside this estimate.
guide.sourceCode: Código do Trabalho, arts. 239, 263 and 264: holiday duration, Christmas allowance and holiday allowance
guide.reviewed: Rules reviewed on 19 November 2026. The separate withholding on each payment of a month was checked in the original text of Despacho n.º 233-A/2026, and the Código do Trabalho articles in consolidated-text copies. The 22-working-day reference for the holiday allowance is common practice, not stated in those texts. Withholding each twelfth at the effective rate of the whole allowance (Lei n.º 11/2013, art. 3) is the usual payroll practice; that law was not checked against its text. The 11% Social Security rate was checked against secondary sources.

help.baseMonthly: The base pay (retribuição base) in euros a month, before Social Security and IRS. Do not include allowances, bonuses or overtime.
help.seniorityPay: Diuturnidades are supplements paid for length of service. Enter 0 if you have none.
help.startDate: The day the permanent contract began. For a company group or a previous contract with the same employer, check how your seniority is counted.

Expiry is the end of a fixed-term contract, of certain or uncertain term (arts. 344 and 345 of the Código do Trabalho). It is not due when the contract ends because you declared you would not renew it.

help.fixedTermKind: It sets the maximum duration: 2 years with a certain term, 4 with an uncertain term (art. 148). The compensation is the same, 24 days a year.
help.renewals: How many times the contract was renewed. A certain-term contract can be renewed at most three times (art. 149(4)). Leave it empty if it never was.

help.earlierMonths: Earlier fixed-term contracts or temporary agency work in the same job, and service contracts for the same work, with the same employer or a company in its group. They count towards the maximum duration (art. 148(6)). Leave it empty if there were none.

dismissalCompensation.scope: Covers collective dismissal, extinction of the post and unsuitability on a permanent contract. Not covered: dismissal with just cause, unlawful dismissal, mutual agreement and the public sector. For the end of a fixed-term contract, choose expiry of a fixed-term contract.

guide.example: Someone earning {{base}} a month plus {{seniorityPay}} of diuturnidades, with a contract that began on {{start}} and ended on {{end}}, has {{seniority}} years of seniority. The daily amount is {{daily}}. The contract began between 1 November 2011 and 30 September 2013, so {{twentyYears}} years up to 30 September 2013 count 20 days ({{twentyAmount}}), {{eighteenYears}} years complete the first three years at 18 days ({{eighteenAmount}}), {{twelveYears}} years up to 30 April 2023 count 12 days ({{twelveAmount}}) and the last {{fourteenYears}} years count 14 days ({{fourteenAmount}}). The total is {{total}}, below the cap of {{cap}}.
guide.methodBase: The base is the monthly base pay plus diuturnidades. The daily amount is that monthly amount divided by 30.
guide.methodRates: For seniority from 1 May 2023, the compensation is 14 days of base pay and diuturnidades per full year (art. 366(1) of the Código do Trabalho, as amended by Lei n.º 13/2023). Seniority before that date keeps the earlier rate: 12 days a year from 1 October 2013.
guide.methodTransitional: Older contracts keep the earlier rates for the time already worked (art. 5 of Lei n.º 69/2013). Before 1 November 2011: one month per year until 31 October 2012, then 20 days a year until 30 September 2013. From 1 November 2011 to 30 September 2013: 20 days a year until 30 September 2013. From 1 October 2013 to 30 April 2023 every contract counts 12 days a year, except that the first three years of seniority count 18 days when the contract was less than three years old on 1 October 2013. From 1 May 2023 every year counts 14 days.
guide.methodCaps: The monthly amount cannot exceed 20 times the minimum wage ({{baseCap}} with the 2026 minimum wage of {{rmmg}}), and the whole compensation cannot exceed 12 monthly amounts, at most {{totalCapRmmg}} (240 times the minimum wage). When the part up to 30 September 2013 already reaches that cap, the later periods are not added.
guide.methodFraction: An incomplete year counts proportionally: the calculator counts whole anniversaries of the start date plus the days since the last one over the days of that year. The termination date counts as a day worked.
guide.methodTax: Information only, not part of the figure: part of a termination payment can be excluded from IRS under art. 2(4) of the CIRS, up to a limit tied to your regular pay over the last 12 months and your years of seniority. The rest is taxable income. Ask the Tax Authority or an accountant for the exact limit in your case.
guide.methodBudget: The compensation is a one-off amount. Spreading it over your upcoming months, together with any unemployment benefit you are entitled to, shows how long it covers your spending.
guide.supported: Collective dismissal, extinction of the post and unsuitability of the worker on a permanent contract, and the expiry of a fixed-term contract of certain or uncertain term, with termination in 2026.
guide.unsupportedFixedTerm: Fixed-term contracts that expired before 1 May 2023 (18 days a year under the earlier text), early termination of a fixed-term contract, and expiry caused by the worker's own declaration.
guide.unsupportedJustCause: Dismissal with just cause (disciplinary), which follows different rules.
guide.unsupportedUnlawful: Unlawful dismissal, where the court sets the compensation, in general between 15 and 45 days of base pay per year of seniority.
guide.unsupportedAgreement: Termination by mutual agreement, where the amount is negotiated and there is no legal formula.
guide.unsupportedPublic: Public-sector workers, who follow different rules.
guide.sourceLaw69: Lei n.º 69/2013, of 30 August (Diário da República): new wording of art. 366 and the transitional regimes of arts. 5 and 6
guide.sourceCode: Código do Trabalho, consolidated text (Diário da República): arts. 147, 148, 149, 344, 345 and 366
guide.reviewed: Rules reviewed on 20 November 2026 against the Diário da República: the consolidated Código do Trabalho (arts. 147, 148, 149, 344, 345 and 366), Lei n.º 93/2019 (arts. 11 and 13), Lei n.º 13/2023 (art. 35) and Lei n.º 69/2013 (arts. 5 and 6), with the 2026 minimum wage of 920 euros (Decreto-Lei n.º 139/2025). The 14 days count only for seniority from 1 May 2023, as art. 35(2) of Lei n.º 13/2023 sets. The 24 days of a fixed-term expiry count for the whole contract: that reading of art. 35(1) is the one in the IGeFE note, and a court could read it differently for contracts signed before 1 May 2023. Educational, not legal advice.
guide.methodFixedTerm: Expiry of a fixed-term contract (arts. 344(2) and 345(4) of the Código do Trabalho, as amended by Lei n.º 13/2023): 24 days of base pay and diuturnidades per full year of seniority, calculated as in art. 366. The daily amount, the 20 times minimum wage cap on the monthly amount, the cap of 12 monthly amounts and the proportional fraction of a year all apply. Art. 35(1) of Lei n.º 13/2023 submits contracts signed before 1 May 2023 to the new text, and its art. 35(2) limits only the 14 days of art. 366(1) to the time from that date. The IGeFE note of 5 July 2023 reads this as 24 days for every contract that expires from 1 May 2023: its example of a contract from 1 September 2021 to 31 August 2023 counts all 730 days at 24 days. So the whole duration counts at 24 days, and the rates of permanent contracts (12, 14, 18 and 20 days) do not apply. A fixed-term contract lasts at most two years, or four with an uncertain term (art. 148), so one that keeps to those limits and expires in 2026 was not signed before 1 October 2013 and the transitional rules of art. 6 of Lei n.º 69/2013 do not apply.
guide.sourceLaw13Text: Lei n.º 13/2023, of 3 April (Diário da República): new wording of arts. 344(2), 345(4) and 366(1) of the Código do Trabalho and art. 35 on its application in time
guide.sourceIgefe: IGeFE, Nota Informativa n.º 10/2023 (5 July 2023): 24 days for every fixed-term contract that expires from 1 May 2023, whatever its signing date
guide.methodDurationLimit: Maximum duration (art. 148 of the Código do Trabalho, as amended by Lei n.º 93/2019): 2 years with a certain term, renewals included, and 4 years with an uncertain term. A certain-term contract can be renewed up to three times, and the renewals together cannot last longer than the first period (art. 149(4)). Earlier fixed-term contracts and temporary agency work in the same job, and service contracts for the same work, with the same employer also count towards the 2 years (art. 148(6)). Contracts signed before 1 October 2019 keep the earlier limits (art. 11(4) of Lei n.º 93/2019): 3 years with a certain term (18 months for a first job seeker and 2 years in the other cases of art. 140(4)) and 6 years with an uncertain term; the calculator takes the start date as the signing date. When the dates pass the limit, the calculator warns that the contract would likely be open-ended (art. 147(2)(b)) and that ending it would be a dismissal, but still shows the expiry figure. For a certain-term contract you can also enter the number of renewals, the length of the first period and the months of earlier contracts for the same job, and the warning then covers those rules too: more than three renewals, renewals longer in total than the first period (art. 147(2)(a)), or earlier contracts that bring the 2-year limit forward. Contracts signed before 1 October 2019 could be renewed three times with no limit on how long the renewals last (initial wording of art. 148(1)), and earlier contracts count towards their 3 years (initial wording of art. 148(5)). Earlier contracts do not count towards the limit of an uncertain term.
guide.sourceLaw93: Lei n.º 93/2019, of 4 September (Diário da República): new wording of arts. 148 and 149 of the Código do Trabalho, its application in time (art. 11(4)) and entry into force on 1 October 2019 (art. 13)
guide.sourceArt148: Código do Trabalho, art. 148 (Diário da República), with its initial 2009 wording: the limits for contracts signed before 1 October 2019

before2019.uncertain: A fixed-term contract signed before 1 October 2019 keeps the earlier limits (art. 11(4) of Lei n.º 93/2019): at most 6 years with an uncertain term (initial wording of art. 148(4)). With these dates, the limit was reached on {{date}}.

durationWarning.consequence: A contract that passes its maximum duration or the renewal limits converts into an open-ended contract (art. 147(2)(a) and (b)), with seniority counted from the first day (art. 147(3)). Ending it is then a dismissal, not an expiry, with different compensation rules; an employer that ends it only by letting the term run out may be dismissing unlawfully. The figure here is still the expiry compensation.
durationWarning.action: Calculate as a dismissal on a permanent contract

earlier.from2019: The limit counts {{months}} of earlier contracts for the same job with the same employer (art. 148(6)).
earlier.before2019: The limit counts {{months}} of earlier contracts for the same job with the same employer (initial wording of art. 148(5)).

renewals.from2019: A certain-term contract can be renewed at most three times (art. 149(4) of the Código do Trabalho, as amended by Lei n.º 93/2019). This one was renewed {{count}} times.
renewals.before2019: A certain-term contract signed before 1 October 2019 can be renewed at most three times (initial wording of art. 148(1), kept by art. 11(4) of Lei n.º 93/2019). This one was renewed {{count}} times.

durationWarning.renewalLength: The renewals together cannot last longer than the first period (art. 149(4)). With a first period of {{months}}, the contract could run until {{date}} at most.

guide.example: Someone earning {{gross}} a month on average (today's euros, 14 payments), with {{years}} years of contributions, retiring at {{age}}. The statutory pension is {{statutory}} a month, a global formation rate of {{rate}}. Retiring {{months}} months before the normal age deducts {{penalty}} and applies the sustainability factor, leaving {{monthly}} a month gross, or {{replacement}} of the salary. After IRS the pension is {{netPension}} a month. Against an estimated net pay of {{net}}, the gap is {{gap}} a month.
guide.methodReferenceBody: The reference remuneration is the average of your yearly pay over the whole career, revalued with consumer-price coefficients and divided by 14. The calculator works in today's euros: you enter an average real monthly salary and the result is also in today's euros.
guide.methodRateBody: The annual rate depends on slices of the reference remuneration in multiples of the IAS ({{ias}} in 2026): {{rates}} for the slices up to 1.1, up to 2, up to 4, up to 8 and above 8 times the IAS. Careers of up to 20 years use a flat 2%. The rate is multiplied by the years of contributions, at most 40, to give the global formation rate.
guide.methodAgesBody: The normal age of access to the old-age pension is {{normal2026}} in 2026 and has been set at {{normal2027}} for 2027. The calculator uses the 2026 value.
guide.methodEarlyBody: Before the normal age, from age 60 with at least 15 years of contributions, each month of anticipation takes off {{penalty}}, and the 2026 sustainability factor ({{factor}}, a 17.63% cut) also applies. The two multiply. Exemptions, such as very long careers, are not modelled.
guide.methodLateBody: After the normal age, up to 70, each month adds a bonus that depends on the years of contributions: 0.33% from 15 years, 0.50% from 25, 0.65% from 35 and 1% from 40. The pension with the bonus cannot exceed 92% of the reference remuneration.
guide.methodMinimumBody: If the formula gives less than the 2026 minimum pension for your career, the minimum is shown instead: {{min15}} for 15 to 20 years, {{min21}} for 21 to 30 and {{min31}} for 31 or more. The minimum does not apply to early retirement.
guide.methodGapBody: The gap compares the net pension with your net pay today, both per payment over 14 payments. Net pay is the gross salary minus 11% Social Security and the 2026 IRS withholding for a single person without dependants on the mainland. The net pension is the estimated gross pension minus IRS withheld under the 2026 pension table VIII (Despacho n.º 233-A/2026, unmarried holder or married with two earners, without disability); pensions pay no Social Security and pensions up to 920 euros a month have no withholding. The final IRS depends on your whole income and deductions.
guide.methodBudgetBody: Read the gap as the monthly amount your savings and investments would have to cover. It moves with every assumption above.
guide.unsupportedMixed: Careers that began before 2002 (mixed formula, with the older rules for the years up to 2001). This calculator only covers the whole-career formula for people who started contributing in 2002 or later.
guide.unsupportedSpecial: Pay that varies a lot over the career, gaps in contributions and careers longer than 40 years.
guide.unsupportedCga: Civil servants in the CGA, self-employed workers and other special regimes.
guide.unsupportedOther: Early-retirement regimes without penalty, disability pensions and updates to the pension after retirement.
guide.sourceLaw: Decreto-Lei n.º 187/2007, as amended (Diário da República)
guide.sourceAges: Portaria n.º 476/2025/1: normal age for 2027 and sustainability factor for 2026
guide.sourceMinimum: Portaria n.º 480-B/2025/1: 2026 pension update and minimum pensions
guide.sourceSimulator: Segurança Social Direta: official pension simulator
guide.reviewed: Rules and 2026 values reviewed on 19 November 2026 against Decreto-Lei n.º 187/2007 and the 2026 portarias. The accrual rates, the bonus and the minimum pensions were cross-checked in secondary sources and the Segurança Social pages, not read in the consolidated law, and the simplifications above are ours. The pension withholding table VIII was checked row by row on 20 November 2026 against the annex of Despacho n.º 233-A/2026 as published in the Diário da República.
guide.sourceWithholding: Despacho n.º 233-A/2026 (Diário da República): the 2026 IRS withholding tables, including pension table VIII

read.title: How to read the result
read.intro: This calculator looks backwards. It takes the yearly returns of the S&P 500 (S&P Composite index data) between the years you choose and applies them to your amount. The data covers {{first}} to {{last}}.
read.future: It is not a forecast. To project an index forward with your own return and fee assumptions, use the index projection on the investment return page.

example.title: Worked example
example.setup: Invest {{initial}} on 1 January {{start}} and leave it until 31 December {{end}} ({{years}} years), with dividends reinvested and no further contributions. The data turns it into {{finalTotal}}, a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of {{cagrTotal}}.
example.price: Without dividends (price return only) the same amount ends at {{finalPrice}}, or {{cagrPrice}} a year. The gap is what reinvested dividends added.
example.real: Measured in {{start}} dollars, after removing US inflation, the final value is {{finalReal}}, or {{cagrReal}} a year.
example.range: The path was rough: the best year of the range was {{bestYear}} ({{bestReturn}}) and the worst {{worstYear}} ({{worstReturn}}).

method.title: How it is calculated
method.intro: For every year in your range the calculator does the same four things:

steps.a: It adds the money invested on 1 January: your initial amount in the first year and the yearly contribution in every year.
steps.b: It grows the balance by that year's return: the total return if dividends are reinvested, the price return if not.
steps.c: If you ask for inflation-adjusted values, it divides by US consumer prices (CPI), so every figure is in the start year's dollars. Contributions are deflated with the prices of the day they are made.
steps.d: It records the value at 31 December for the table and the chart.

method.cagr: The CAGR is the geometric mean of the yearly returns in the range, in the terms you chose. It describes the index over those years and does not depend on how much you contribute.
method.contributions: Yearly contributions are added on 1 January, before that year's return, so they earn the whole year.
method.limits: The first year in the data is {{first}} and the last complete year is {{last}}. Each amount is capped at {{maxAmount}}.

data.title: Data and method
data.source: Returns are computed by WonderMoney from the year-end S&P 500 level and the dividends in Aswath Damodaran's dataset "Historical Returns on Stocks, Bonds and Bills" (NYU Stern), downloaded on {{downloaded}}. Inflation comes from the consumer price index (CPI) in Robert J. Shiller's public dataset "U.S. Stock Markets 1871-Present and CAPE Ratio" (Yale University), downloaded on {{shillerDownloaded}}.
data.method: For each calendar year the price return is the year-end level divided by the previous year-end level, minus one. The total return adds the year's dividends to the year-end level before dividing, which treats the dividends as reinvested at the year end. Inflation is the change in the CPI between the same two Decembers.
data.check: As a check, every year's total return was compared with the total return Damodaran publishes himself, and none differs by more than 0.1 percentage point. Because years run from year-end to year-end, they line up with the calendar-year figures usually quoted for the index.
data.trademark: "S&P 500" and "S&P Composite" only name the index. This page shows yearly values derived from public academic data and no daily prices, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by S&P Dow Jones Indices.

items.fxBody: Returns are in US dollars. If you invest from the euro area, the euro-dollar exchange rate adds to or takes away from these figures, sometimes by several points a year. Currency risk is separate from the market's.
items.feesBody: Fund fees, brokerage charges and spreads are not deducted. A fund that tracks the index returns the index minus its costs.
items.taxesBody: Tax on dividends and gains is not included, and it depends on where you live.
items.sequenceBody: This is one large US index in one country's history. Other markets and periods did far worse, and moving the start or end by a few years can change the result a lot.
items.past: Past performance does not predict future returns. This tool is educational and is not investment advice.

read.monthly: The figures here are monthly averages, with the latest for {{month}}. They are not the daily rate: the rate that sets your payment is the one fixed on the date your contract uses.

read.title: How to read this page
read.estimator: The estimator prices one 30-day month on the regulated tariff: the contracted power charge, the energy you use, the audiovisual contribution and the electricity tax, then adds VAT line by line at the rate that applies to each.
read.index: The index view looks at all household bills, not just the regulated tariff: Eurostat's average price per kWh in Portugal and in the EU, taxes included, so the two are comparable.
read.market: The regulated tariff is one option. Most households are in the free market, where suppliers set their own prices and offers can be cheaper or dearer than the regulated tariff. The VAT rules are the same in both. The estimator is a reference point, not a recommendation.

example.title: Worked example
example.setup: A household with {{kva}} kVA contracted that uses {{kwh}} kWh in a month on the simple tariff. Power: {{powerPrice}} for 30 days. Energy: {{kwh}} kWh at {{energySimple}}. Plus the audiovisual contribution ({{cav}}) and the electricity tax ({{iec}}). With VAT ({{vatSimple}} in all) the month costs {{totalSimple}}, or {{effective}} once the fixed charges are spread over the kWh.
example.bi: On the bi-hourly tariff ({{energyPeak}} outside off-peak, {{energyValley}} in off-peak hours) with half the consumption in off-peak hours, the same month costs {{totalBi}}.
example.power: Contracted power matters too: at 6.9 kVA and 300 kWh the month costs {{totalBigger}}, because a higher power has a higher daily charge and its power term pays the full VAT rate.

method.title: How it is calculated
method.intro: For one 30-day month the estimator does the same five things:

steps.a: Power: the daily price for your contracted power, times 30 days.
steps.b: Energy: your kWh at the simple price, or split between the two bi-hourly prices by the share you enter.
steps.c: Audiovisual contribution (CAV): a fixed monthly amount, with reduced VAT. Households that use less than 400 kWh a year are exempt.
steps.d: Electricity consumption tax (IEC): a fixed amount per kWh, with the standard VAT rate.
steps.e: VAT on each line, then the sum. The result is rounded to the cent at the end.

method.vat: VAT rules, as ERSE explains them: the reduced rate ({{reduced}}) applies to the first {{allowance}} kWh of energy in 30 days ({{allowanceLarge}} kWh for households of five or more) for contracted power up to 6.9 kVA, to the network-access part of the power term (the fixed term of the access tariff ERSE sets) for contracted power up to 3.45 kVA, and to the audiovisual contribution. Everything else pays {{standard}}.
method.bi: Bi-hourly versus simple: the simple price is {{energySimple}}, against {{energyPeak}} outside off-peak and {{energyValley}} in off-peak hours. On energy alone the two cost the same when {{breakEven}}% of the consumption is in off-peak hours. With a lower share simple is cheaper, with a higher one bi-hourly is.
method.days: The reduced-VAT allowance is per 30 days, the period used here. A real bill for a longer or shorter period scales the allowance by its number of days.

data.title: Data and sources
data.tariffs: Regulated tariffs: ERSE (Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos), the transitional sales tariffs for low-voltage households up to 20.7 kVA in mainland Portugal, in force since {{from}}, plus the audiovisual contribution, electricity tax and VAT rules from ERSE's own documents. Read on {{checked}}. ERSE can change the energy price every quarter.
data.eurostat: Price index: Eurostat, "Electricity prices for household consumers - bi-annual data" (nrg_pc_204), band DC (2,500 to 4,999 kWh a year), all taxes and levies included, in euro per kWh, from {{firstPeriod}} to {{lastPeriod}}. Eurostat updated the dataset on {{updated}} and this page's copy was built on {{fetched}}.
data.vatLink: ERSE, VAT on the electricity bill
data.refresh: The page reads two saved data files and never calls these sources while you use it. Both carry their date and are refreshed by hand.

limits.title: What these figures leave out

items.market: Free market: most offers are not the regulated tariff. They can be cheaper or dearer, with different prices, discounts and conditions. Compare with a real simulator before you decide.
items.dgeg: The small monthly DGEG fee is not included because we could not confirm its amount in an ERSE document, and nor is any meter or other charge. Check your own bill for the exact total.
items.scope: The estimator covers mainland Portugal and 3.45 to 6.9 kVA of contracted power. Higher powers, the Azores and Madeira have other tariffs and VAT rates.
items.social: The social electricity tariff, a discount for eligible households, is not applied. Ask your supplier or ERSE if you may be entitled.
items.average: The index compares averages for one consumption band. Your own price depends on your contract, power and hours of use, and Portugal's average blends regulated and free-market contracts.
items.education: Educational use only, not advice to choose or change supplier.

use.title: How to use the comparison
use.quick: Quick mode needs only your contracted power and your monthly bill or kWh. A bill in euro is turned into kWh by working back the regulated tariff's bill, taxes included, as ERSE's quick simulation does.
use.full: Full mode takes the kWh of each period from your invoice, or a total for any number of days split across the periods with the E-REDES standard profile for your power and consumption.
use.diagram: You can also give it your E-REDES consumption file, downloaded from Balcão Digital. Its 15-minute readings give your real kWh in each period and cycle. The file is read in your browser and never sent anywhere.
use.mine: Under "Compare with my tariff" you enter the prices on your invoice. Your tariff then goes through the same calculation as every offer, so the saving shown on each one is like for like.
use.solar: Under "Solar panels" you add a system by district capital or by coordinates, with its tilt, orientation, peak power and losses. Its production is subtracted from your consumption hour by hour, and the offers are ranked on what you still buy from the grid. The summary shows the share used at home, the surplus and what the panels save on the cheapest offer. A surplus sale price, if you enter one, is shown apart from the ranking.
use.options: At the top of the results, the cheapest simple, bi-hourly and tri-hourly offers on the same consumption show whether another option would pay off. The filters narrow the list, and the CSV button downloads it.

method.title: How it is calculated
method.intro: Each offer is priced the way ERSE's simulator does it (Manual do Simulador de Preços de Energia, June 2026):

steps.a: Power: the price per day times the days.
steps.b: Energy: the kWh of each period times its price.
steps.c: Social tariff: ERSE's discount on power and energy, up to 6.9 kVA.
steps.d: The audiovisual contribution and the electricity tax, at their legal amounts.
steps.e: Mandatory services, refunds and discounts any client gets, and the new-client discount in the first year, as each offer reports them to ERSE.
steps.f: VAT at the reduced and standard rates, as set out below.
steps.g: A year is the same consumption over 365 days; "later years" leaves out the new-client discount.

method.vat: VAT is {{reduced}} on the audiovisual contribution, on the network-access part of the power price up to 3.45 kVA, and on the first {{allowance}} kWh every 30 days up to 6.9 kVA ({{allowanceLarge}} kWh for a household of five or more). Everything else pays {{standard}}.
method.month: A month is a twelfth of a year, {{days}} days, as in ERSE's simulator, so a year is exactly twelve months.
method.split: When only a total is known, it is split across the periods with the E-REDES consumption profile of the household's class: A above 13.8 kVA, otherwise B above 7,140 kWh a year and C below it.

data.title: Data and sources
data.erse: Offers: ERSE's price simulator, the export of {{date}}, with {{offers}} offers from {{suppliers}} suppliers and the regulated tariff. Suppliers must report their household offers to ERSE. Prices are before VAT and taxes; the page adds them.
data.refresh: The page takes a new export from ERSE every week. Offers that have ended by then are left out.
data.names: ERSE gives each supplier as a code; the page shows the brand name each supplier uses on its own website.
data.solar: Solar production: PVGIS {{pvgisVersion}}, from the European Commission's Joint Research Centre, with the {{pvgisDatabase}} radiation database ({{pvgisFrom}}–{{pvgisTo}}). For each district capital the page holds PVGIS's typical year, hour by hour, for 1 kWp facing south at the optimal tilt with 14 % losses, downloaded on {{pvgisDate}}. Another tilt, orientation or exact coordinates are sent, through the WonderMoney server, to PVGIS, which calculates the same typical year for them; if it does not answer, the nearest district capital's table is used and the page says so. Without an E-REDES file, your consumption's hours are rebuilt from the standard profile's split across the periods in each month.
data.manualLink: ERSE, Manual do Simulador de Preços de Energia (June 2026)

limits.title: What the totals leave out

items.a: The DGEG fee, a few cents a month, and any meter or other charges.
items.b: Personal negotiation: the prices are the published ones.
items.c: Indexed offers are priced at ERSE's estimate for the coming months. If you choose OMIE prices, those whose supplier publishes its formula show what they would have cost over the last 12 months (or on your file's dates), not what they will cost: what you pay follows the market.
items.d: Dual offers can include gas in their fixed amounts; they are left out unless you include them.
items.e: With a bill or a total, the split across periods is the standard profile, not your own. The E-REDES file gives your real split.
items.solar: Solar production is a typical year, at the district capital or at your coordinates rounded to about 5 km: shade and a given year's weather change it.
items.f: This is an educational estimate, not advice. Check the offer's standard sheet and terms before you sign.

read.title: How to read this page
read.prices: The top of the page shows the latest national average price per litre of diesel, petrol 95 and autogas, as published by DGEG for {{asOf}}, and how far each moved in a week: diesel {{dieselChange}} and petrol {{gasolineChange}} against the previous week.
read.calculator: The calculator turns your driving into a monthly fuel cost. You give the distance, the consumption in litres per 100 km and the fuel; the price starts at the latest average and you can change it to the price you really pay.
read.noForecast: This page does not forecast. It shows what DGEG measured and what your driving costs at that price; it does not say what the price will be next week.
read.stations: Below them are the cheapest stations: the {{stationsDistrict}} cheapest of mainland Portugal or of a district, or the {{stationsMunicipality}} cheapest of a municipality, for the fuel you choose. Each shows the price, the station and its brand, the address, a map link and when the station last updated the price.

example.title: Worked example
example.setup: A diesel car driven {{distance}} a month using {{consumption}}, at the latest average of {{price}}. Fuel used: {{distance}} times {{consumption}} divided by 100 is {{litres}}. Cost: {{litres}} times {{price}} is {{monthly}} a month, about {{yearly}} a year, or {{per100}} for every 100 km.
example.trips: Distance can also be a trip. A 40 km round trip made 20 times a month with the same car costs {{tripCost}} each time, {{tripMonthly}} a month.

method.title: How it is calculated

steps.a: Distance a month: the distance you give, a week counted as 52 divided by 12 weeks a month, or a trip multiplied by trips a month.
steps.b: Litres: distance times consumption divided by 100.
steps.c: Cost: litres times the price per litre you enter, rounded to the cent.

method.change: The week-on-week change is the latest DGEG average minus the one seven days earlier, in euro per litre and as a percentage of the earlier price.
method.stations: The cheapest stations are DGEG's station prices sorted from lowest to highest; on a tie the more recently updated price comes first. Prices not updated for 30 days, and prices far outside the usual range (most likely a typing error), are left out. The median is the middle price of all stations in the area, and the saving on a tank is the median minus the cheapest price, times 50 litres.

data.title: Data and sources
data.dgeg: Prices: DGEG (Direção-Geral de Energia e Geologia), Preço Médio Diário of road fuels in mainland Portugal, for gasóleo simples, gasolina simples 95 and GPL auto. The latest day is {{asOf}}; this page's copy was built on {{fetched}}. The history is one DGEG value every seven days back to {{first}}, copied as DGEG publishes it.
data.terms: DGEG states that this information is free and may be used freely, provided DGEG is named as the source, the date of the latest update is shown and the information is reproduced faithfully. The prices are reported by the stations, which are responsible for them.
data.dgegLink: DGEG, daily average price (Preço Médio Diário)
data.refresh: The page reads one saved data file and never calls DGEG while you use it. The file is refreshed by a script that refuses data that is stale or implausible, so a failed refresh keeps the last good numbers and their date ({{asOf}}).
data.stations: Stations: DGEG's prices per station, as the stations report them, for the same three fuels. The snapshot was taken on {{stationsDate}} at {{stationsTime}} UTC, and each price keeps the date and time the station last updated it.
data.stationsRefresh: The station list is a snapshot taken once a day, when the site is rebuilt, not a live feed. If DGEG does not answer or its data fails the checks, the page keeps the previous snapshot and shows its date ({{stationsDate}}).

items.noForecast: No forecast: nothing here predicts future prices, and past moves do not say where the price goes next.
items.average: National average: it blends all stations in mainland Portugal and is weighted by sales. The price at your station can be higher or lower, and the Azores and Madeira are not included.
items.stations: Stations: the list shows only the few cheapest stations of each area, as DGEG publishes them, and does not rate service or quality. A price can change after the snapshot, so confirm it at the pump.
items.consumption: Consumption: the same figure for every trip. Real consumption changes with speed, load, traffic and the season, and is usually above the official one.
items.scope: Only fuel: tolls, insurance, tax, maintenance and parking are not included. Electric charging is not covered, and other fuels are not shown.

purity.title: Karats and fineness
purity.intro: The purity of gold is given in karats, out of 24, or in thousandths, the number stamped in the hallmark. These are the six legal finenesses of gold in Portugal:

items.k24Body: Pure gold, as in investment bars and coins.
items.k22Body: Gold coins such as the sovereign and the Krugerrand, and much jewellery from India.
items.k19_2Body: Portuguese gold (ouro português), the traditional fineness of Portuguese jewellery.
items.k18Body: The most common fineness of jewellery in Europe.

steps.aBody: NBP's price of a gram of pure gold in zloty, divided by the ECB's zloty per euro of the same day.
steps.bBody: The weight times the fineness divided by 1,000. A 24k piece counts at 999 thousandths.
steps.cBody: The grams of pure gold times the price of a gram of pure gold, rounded to the cent.
steps.dBody: When you enter one, the offer divided by the value, as a percentage, and the difference in euro.

buyers.title: Why buyers pay less than the metal value
buyers.below: A shop that buys gold pays less than the metal value: it melts the piece, pays for assaying and refining, and keeps a margin. How much less varies from shop to shop, so ask more than one and compare each offer with the value here.
buyers.jewellery: New jewellery costs more than its metal value: the price includes the work, the design, the brand and VAT. Selling it later returns the metal at most, not what you paid.
buyers.tips: Before you sell, weigh the piece, check the hallmark, ask for the offer per gram and the fineness the buyer assumed, and keep a written receipt.

data.title: Data and sources
data.nbp: Gold price: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP), the central bank of Poland, publishes each business day the price of 1 g of gold of 1000 fineness that it calculates, in zloty, through its public API. The latest day is {{asOf}}; this page's copy was built on {{fetched}}.
data.why: Why not the LBMA Gold Price: that benchmark, set twice a day in London in US dollars, is administered by ICE Benchmark Administration, which requires a licence to pass it on to others, even delayed. NBP's price is a central bank publication offered to the public through an open API, with no licence or key, so this page uses it and names NBP as the source.
data.ecb: Euro: the ECB euro reference rate for the zloty on the same day, which the European Central Bank publishes for information. A day with only one of the two figures is skipped.
data.ecbLink: ECB, euro reference rate for the Polish zloty
data.refresh: The page reads a saved snapshot and never calls NBP or the ECB while you use it. The site is rebuilt every day with a new snapshot. A refresh that fails or returns implausible figures is refused, and the page keeps the last good price with its date ({{asOf}}).

items.metalBody: The value is the gold content at a reference price. Stones, other metals, the work and the brand are not counted.
items.buyersBody: Buyers pay less, and a shop selling gold charges more.
items.purityBody: The calculator trusts the fineness you choose. An unmarked or gold-plated piece can hold much less gold, or none.
items.referenceBody: NBP's daily price, not a live quote. The market moves during the day.

read.title: How to read this table
read.what: Each broker charges in its own way: a fixed amount or a percentage per order, often with a minimum; a custody fee on what you hold, per month, quarter or half-year; and a fee to convert euros to dollars when you buy US shares. The table writes each fee as the price list does, for an online order, and the calculator applies the same formulas to a whole year.
read.protection: Investor protection covers your securities if the broker fails and cannot return them, up to the amount shown; it never covers a fall in prices. Cash held at a bank is covered by its deposit guarantee instead. The scheme depends on the country of the entity that holds your account, which is why the table names it.
read.notRec: The table is educational. It is not a recommendation, the order is not a ranking, and the cheapest broker for one profile can be the dearest for another. Service, the products on offer and how each broker handles Portuguese tax matter too.

Converting {{converted}} to dollars at {{bankFx}} adds {{bankFxTotal}}, and custody ({{bankCustodyFormula}}) adds {{bankCustody}} with VAT. The year costs {{bankTotal}}, of which {{bankStampDuty}} is stamp duty and {{bankVat}} is VAT.

method.title: Method
method.intro: Every fee was read from the broker's own published price list on the date shown in its row; the whole table was reviewed on {{date}} and is re-checked every quarter. Fees that a price list does not state are marked as not published and left out of the totals, which are then shown as incomplete.

steps.aBody: Each order's commission is the fixed part plus the percentage of the order, then the minimum and the maximum per order. Fees per share count whole shares at the assumed share price. A free monthly allowance is applied month by month.
steps.bBody: For ETF buys, when the option is on and the broker publishes a recurring plan, its fee replaces the order fee.
steps.cBody: US orders pay the broker's conversion fee on the amount converted; fees in dollars are converted at {{rate}} dollars per euro.
steps.dBody: The published formula, per period with its minimum and maximum, is charged on the value held, as many times as there are periods in a year.
steps.eBody: Where the price list says its fees exclude Portuguese stamp duty (4% on brokerage) or VAT (23% on custody), they are added to the fees they apply to.
steps.f: The total adds the year's orders, currency conversion and custody, and the brokers are listed from cheapest to dearest. Brokers missing a fee the profile needs go last.

items.a: Exchange, clearing and regulatory fees that a broker passes on separately, spreads on the price you trade at, and the ongoing charges of the ETF itself.
items.b: Promotions, fee tiers for very active traders, and conditions tied to other products at the bank.
items.c: Selling, transfers out, dividends and the tax on dividends and gains.
items.d: Changes after the date checked: fees change, so the broker's current price list always prevails.

what.title: What a PPR is
what.body: A PPR (plano de poupança-reforma) is a savings product for retirement with its own tax rules: part of what you put in each year can be deducted from your IRS tax, and the money is meant to stay in until retirement or one of the other cases the law sets out. It comes in three legal forms:

forms.fund: An investment fund (fundo de poupança-reforma), supervised by the CMVM. Its value moves with the fund's investments, usually with no guarantee.
forms.linked: Life insurance linked to investment funds, supervised by the ASF. Usually no guarantee of capital or return.
forms.guaranteed: Life insurance not linked to funds, supervised by the ASF. It guarantees the capital, and sometimes a minimum return, under its terms.
forms.pension: A membership of an open pension fund, supervised by the ASF. It may or may not guarantee capital or a return.

what.supervisors: Each supervisor publishes its own list: the CMVM for the funds, the ASF for insurance and pension funds. This page puts both side by side, with each figure as the list states it.

fair.title: Why compare within one risk class
fair.risk: Both supervisors class a product from 1 to 7 by the volatility of its returns, on the same bands: class 1 below 0.5% a year, class 4 from 5% to 10%, class 7 above 25%. A class 6 product can gain more in a good year and lose much more in a bad one than a class 3 product, so a higher past return in a riskier class is not a better result. Compare returns within one class.
fair.returns: Returns are annualised averages over complete calendar years, to the end of {{fundsYear}} for the CMVM funds and of {{insuranceYear}} for the ASF products. They are after the product's yearly costs, but before subscription and redemption fees and tax. Short histories are noisy: a one-year figure says little.
fair.costs: Yearly costs are certain, returns are not. For a fund the figure is its TEC (ongoing charges: management, deposit, audit and supervision fees). For insurance and pension funds the ASF publishes a yearly cost rate of management and deposit fees. The two are close but not identical, so treat small differences across types with care.

example.title: A worked comparison
example.setup: Risk class {{risk}} holds the most products that publish both a yearly cost and a 5-year return: {{count}} of them (of {{total}} PPR in the class).
example.pair: Among them, the lowest yearly cost is {{lowCost}}, for {{lowName}} ({{lowKind}}), with a 5-year annualised return of {{lowReturn}}. The highest is {{highCost}}, for {{highName}} ({{highKind}}), with {{highReturn}}.
example.cost: On {{invested}} invested, that gap in yearly costs is about {{costGap}} a year, every year, whatever the markets do.
example.takeaway: This is an illustration, not a recommendation. Past returns depend on each product's strategy and do not predict future ones, and the two supervisors define yearly costs slightly differently. What the comparison shows is the size of the cost difference within one class of risk.

tax.title: The IRS deduction (EBF, article 21)
tax.deduction: Article 21, n.º 2 of the Estatuto dos Benefícios Fiscais lets each taxpayer (each spouse separately) deduct from the IRS tax {{rate}} of the amounts put into PPR in the year, up to:

limits.under35: {{under35}} a year under 35 (reached with {{full35}} of contributions);

tax.example: The age that counts is the one on 1 January of the year of the contribution (n.º 9). At {{age}}, {{exampleContribution}} contributed in the year gives {{exampleDeduction}}, the full deduction.
tax.conditions: The deduction is part of the overall cap on deductions in article 78, n.º 7 of the IRS code: no cap for the lowest taxable incomes, then from {{capMax}} down to {{capMin}} for the household. It lowers tax due and is not paid out, and contributions made after retirement are not deductible (n.º 10).
tax.payout: When the plan pays out in a case the law allows, a lump sum is taxed on the gain at {{legalRate}} on two fifths of it, an effective {{legalEffective}} of the gain (n.º 3); regular payments are taxed as pensions.

redemption.title: When you can redeem, and what an early redemption costs
redemption.intro: Decreto-Lei n.º 158/2002, article 4, sets out the cases in which you can redeem a PPR without penalty:

cases.unemployment: long-term unemployment of the saver or a member of the household;
cases.incapacity: permanent incapacity for work of the saver or a member of the household;
cases.illness: serious illness of the saver or a member of the household;
cases.mortgage: to pay instalments of a mortgage-backed loan on the saver's own permanent home;
cases.death: the death of the saver, with the value going to the heirs.

redemption.fiveYears: For retirement, age 60 and mortgage payments, each contribution must have been in the plan for at least {{years}} years; the same applies to unemployment, incapacity or illness that already existed when the contribution was made. After {{years}} years from the first contribution, the whole value can be redeemed in those cases if the contributions in the first half of the plan's life were at least {{firstHalf}} of all contributions.
redemption.outside: You can redeem at any other time, under the contract's terms, but then the deductions you had come back as tax, increased by {{clawback}} for each year or part of a year since they were made (EBF article 21, n.º 4), and the gain is taxed at {{otherRate}} rather than the lower rate (n.º 5). If the contributions in the first half of the plan's life were at least {{firstHalf}} of all contributions, that rate applies to four fifths of the gain once the plan has run more than {{reducedAfter}} years and to two fifths after more than {{lowestAfter}}, an effective {{reducedRate}} and {{lowestRate}} (article 5, n.º 3 of the IRS code). Redemption fees in the contract may apply as well.
redemption.transfer: You can move the value to another PPR (article 6); the transfer gives no new deduction. Without a capital or return guarantee no transfer fee can be charged; with one, the fee is at most {{transferFee}} of the value.

method.title: How the comparison is built
method.intro: Two official lists, read as published. Funds: {{funds}} share classes from the CMVM list of {{fundsDate}}. Insurance and pension funds: {{insurance}} products on sale from the ASF platform, read on {{insuranceDate}}.

steps.cmvm: Every share class in the CMVM's list of PPR investment funds for which it publishes a TEC or a return is included, with its manager, fund type, risk class, TEC and annualised returns. The CMVM list publishes no subscription or redemption fees: they are in each fund's IFI, linked on its row.
steps.asf: Every PPR the ASF platform shows as on sale is included: insurance linked to funds, insurance not linked to funds and pension funds, with the minimum and maximum subscription, redemption and transfer fees, the yearly cost rate, the annualised returns, the risk indicator and the capital and return guarantees.
steps.missing: A figure a list leaves out stays "not published"; nothing is estimated. Both lists show 0.00% for horizons a product has no history for, so a run of 0.00% at the longest horizons is read as not published.
steps.refresh: The CMVM figures are refreshed every month from its list. The ASF figures change once a year (reported by 15 April, for the year before) and are refreshed after that. If a refresh fails, the page keeps the last figures with their dates and warns when they are old.

items.closed: PPR no longer on sale, which may still hold savers' money, and pan-European personal pension products (PEPP).
items.fees: Entry and exit fees of the funds (in each IFI), and taxes, which the returns do not include.
items.future: Any forecast. Past returns, risk classes and costs can change, and the supervisors take no responsibility for the figures the managers report.
items.personal: Your situation: how long until you retire, your other savings and how much risk you can take. The investor profile quiz can help with the last one.

savingsGuide.metaTitle: Where to keep your savings in Portugal: products compared | WonderMoney
savingsGuide.metaDescription: Compare savings certificates, treasury certificates, remunerated accounts, savings accounts, term deposits and capitalisation or PPR insurance in Portugal: guarantee, top-ups, withdrawals, interest and IRS.
savingsGuide.title: Where to keep your savings in Portugal
savingsGuide.intro: Seven ways to keep cash in Portugal, side by side: who guarantees the money, whether you can add to it, when you can take it out, how the interest is paid and how IRS applies. Educational only: this page does not recommend any product or provider.
savingsGuide.checked: Facts checked against official sources in {{date}}
savingsGuide.tableCaption: Savings products in Portugal compared by guarantee, top-ups, withdrawals, interest and IRS
savingsGuide.tableHint: Rates, fees and conditions of each product change and vary between providers: always read the terms of the one you consider.

aforro.name: Savings certificates (Certificados de Aforro)
aforro.text: Public debt issued by the Portuguese State and run by IGCP, the Treasury and public debt agency, for people with a Portuguese tax number. Série F lasts up to 15 years. Its rate follows the 3-month Euribor and adds a permanence bonus that grows the longer you hold. Interest accrues every quarter and is added to the balance after IRS. The first purchase is at least 100 units of €1 and later ones at least 10. You can redeem from the first quarterly interest date, losing the interest of the quarter in progress.

tesouro.name: Treasury certificates (Certificados do Tesouro)
tesouro.text: Also State debt run by IGCP, and still on sale in 2026: the new Série 5, open since July 2026, replaced the Poupança Valor series, which no longer takes subscriptions. At launch it paid a fixed rate rising each year, from 2.35% in year one to 3.35% in year ten, with interest paid yearly. The minimum is €1,000 and the maximum €1 million per holder. You can redeem from the end of the first year, losing the interest of the year in progress. Rates for new subscriptions can change.

demand.name: Remunerated current account
demand.text: A current account that pays interest on the balance. The money is available at any time with no loss of interest, but the rate can change and sometimes depends on conditions the bank sets. It is covered by the Deposit Guarantee Fund up to the limit.

savings.name: Savings account
savings.text: A deposit account for savings, often linked to a current account. Some accept transfers straight from another bank, others only from the linked account. Most allow withdrawals at any time, and many without losing interest. It is covered by the Deposit Guarantee Fund up to the limit.

term.name: Term deposit
term.text: You lock in an amount for a set term at a rate agreed upfront. You cannot add to it, and most pay the interest at the end of the term. Early withdrawal is allowed by only some, and usually costs half or more of the interest accrued. It is covered by the Deposit Guarantee Fund up to the limit.

capitalisation.name: Capitalisation insurance
capitalisation.text: A life insurance contract that accumulates savings. The guarantee is the insurer's, not the Deposit Guarantee Fund's, and whether capital is guaranteed depends on the contract, so check it. Most charge a fee on early withdrawal in the first years. The gain is taxed when you withdraw, and the rate falls the longer you hold.

ppr.name: PPR insurance (retirement savings plan)
ppr.text: A retirement savings plan sold here as insurance. Like capitalisation insurance, the guarantee is the insurer's and depends on the contract. Early withdrawal carries a fee in the first years unless it is for a reason set out in law, such as retirement, long-term unemployment, serious illness or permanent incapacity. Deducting contributions in your IRS return comes with conditions: see the tax section.

cells.certificatesTopUp: Only additional subscriptions: pay by entity and reference in the CTT app, pay the State through AforroNet, or pay at a CTT counter
cells.demandTopUp: Top up the balance, directly by transfer from another bank
