fgd.title: The Deposit Guarantee Fund
fgd.p1: The Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos (FGD) repays deposits at its member banks, up to €100,000 per depositor and per bank, if a bank cannot pay.
fgd.p2: It covers current, savings and term deposits. The limit is per bank: balances you hold at the same bank add up to one €100,000 limit, while balances at different banks are each covered up to their own limit.
fgd.p3: It does not cover savings or treasury certificates, which are State debt, nor insurance, which relies on the insurer. An account at a bank in another country is usually covered by that country's scheme, not the Portuguese one.

tax.title: How IRS applies
tax.intro: Interest and gains from savings are capital income (category E of IRS). The rules differ by product.

domestic.title: Certificates and Portuguese banks
domestic.text: Interest is taxed by withholding at source at 28%, a final rate (CIRS art. 71). You can choose to add it to the rest of your income instead (englobamento), in which case the amount withheld counts as a payment on account.

foreign.title: Foreign banks
foreign.text: A bank abroad does not withhold Portuguese tax. If you are resident in Portugal you must declare the interest in your IRS return, where it is taxed at 28% unless you choose englobamento (CIRS art. 72).

insurance.title: Capitalisation insurance
insurance.text: The gain is taxed when you withdraw, at 28%. If you held the contract for more than 5 and up to 8 years, a fifth of the gain is excluded (22.4%), and after 8 years three fifths are (11.2%). These reductions apply only if at least 35% of the premiums were paid in the first half of the contract (CIRS art. 5(3)).

ppr.title: PPR
ppr.text: If you withdraw for a reason set out in law, the gain is taxed at 8% (20% on two fifths of it). Outside those cases the gain is taxed at 21.5%, reduced to 17.2% once the plan has run more than 5 years and to 8.6% after more than 8 (21.5% on four fifths and then on two fifths of the gain), if at least 35% of contributions were paid in the first half of the plan's life. You also give back what you deducted in your IRS return, plus 10% for each year or part of a year, except on the holder's death or when the contribution has been in the plan for at least 5 years and the withdrawal is for a reason set out in law (EBF art. 21 and CIRS art. 5(3)).

netWorthTracker.whatTitle: What Is Net Worth and Why Does It Matter?
netWorthTracker.whatBody1: Your net worth is the single most important number in personal finance. It is the difference between everything you own (assets) and everything you owe (liabilities). Unlike income, which tells you how much flows in, net worth tells you how much wealth you have actually accumulated.
netWorthTracker.whatBody2: Most people have a rough sense of their income. Almost nobody knows their net worth — because calculating it means pulling data from every bank account, every broker, every loan. WonderMoney does this automatically.
netWorthTracker.formulaLabel: Net Worth = Total Assets − Total Liabilities
netWorthTracker.howTitle: How WonderMoney Tracks Your Net Worth
netWorthTracker.how1Body: Link your bank accounts via Open Banking (PSD2). Balances sync automatically every day — current accounts, savings, credit cards, loans.
netWorthTracker.how2Body: Market values are updated regularly as data becomes available.
netWorthTracker.how3Body: WonderMoney adds everything together: bank balances + portfolio value − liabilities = your real net worth, updated every morning.

howToCalculateNetWorth.metaTitle: How to Calculate Net Worth — Complete Guide | WonderMoney
howToCalculateNetWorth.metaDescription: Learn how to calculate your net worth step by step. What to include, what to exclude, and how to track it over time. Free net worth tracker included.
howToCalculateNetWorth.heroTitle: How to Calculate Your Net Worth
howToCalculateNetWorth.heroSubtitle: Net worth is the single most important number in personal finance. Here is exactly how to calculate it — and how to track it automatically.
howToCalculateNetWorth.whatBody: Net worth is the difference between everything you own (assets) and everything you owe (liabilities). It is the financial equivalent of a balance sheet — a snapshot of where you stand right now.
howToCalculateNetWorth.formulaLabel: Net Worth = Total Assets − Total Liabilities
howToCalculateNetWorth.whyTitle: Why Net Worth Matters More Than Income
howToCalculateNetWorth.whyBody: Income tells you how much flows in. Net worth tells you how much you have actually kept. Two people with the same salary can have wildly different net worths depending on their spending habits, debt levels, and investment decisions. Net worth is the scoreboard that actually matters.
howToCalculateNetWorth.assetsBody: Assets are everything you own that has financial value. Be thorough — most people underestimate their assets by forgetting certain categories.
howToCalculateNetWorth.assetCategory3Items: Market value of any property you own (not the purchase price)
howToCalculateNetWorth.assetNote: Use current market value, not purchase price or sentimental value. Your pension pot counts — check your most recent statement.
howToCalculateNetWorth.liabilitiesBody: Liabilities are everything you owe. Include the outstanding balance, not the original loan amount.
howToCalculateNetWorth.liabilityCategory1Items: Outstanding balance on any property loan
howToCalculateNetWorth.liabilityCategory2Items: Car loans, personal loans, credit card balances
howToCalculateNetWorth.liabilityCategory4Items: BNPL balances, money owed to friends or family
howToCalculateNetWorth.calculateTitle: Step 3: Subtract to Get Your Number
howToCalculateNetWorth.calculateBody: Once you have both totals, the calculation is straightforward: subtract total liabilities from total assets. The result is your net worth. It can be positive or negative — negative is common early in life when mortgage and student loan balances dominate.
howToCalculateNetWorth.trackBody: A one-time calculation is useful. Monthly tracking is transformative. Watching your net worth grow month by month makes the impact of your saving and investment decisions visible. It also reveals problems early — months where net worth shrinks despite stable income are a signal worth investigating.
howToCalculateNetWorth.autoBody: Doing this manually every month requires pulling data from every bank, broker, and loan account. WonderMoney connects directly to your bank accounts via Open Banking and imports your investment portfolio, then calculates and updates your net worth every day automatically — no spreadsheet required.
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq1Q: Should I include my pension in net worth?
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq1A: Yes. Your pension pot is an asset. Include the current value from your most recent pension statement. It is illiquid, but it is real wealth.
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq2Q: Should I include my home in net worth?
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq2A: Include your home at current market value (not purchase price), then subtract the outstanding mortgage as a liability. The difference — your equity — is part of your net worth.
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq3Q: How often should I calculate my net worth?
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq3A: Monthly is ideal. It is frequent enough to spot trends and react to changes, but not so frequent that short-term market fluctuations cause unnecessary anxiety.
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq4Q: What is a good net worth by age?
howToCalculateNetWorth.faq4A: There is no universal answer — it depends on income, country, family situation, and goals. A useful benchmark: aim for net worth equal to 1x your annual income by age 30, 3x by 40, and 6x by 50.
howToCalculateNetWorth.ctaBody: Connect your accounts and WonderMoney calculates your complete net worth every day. No spreadsheets. Free and open source.

featureBudgeting.heroTitle: Budget Every Euro Before You Spend It
featureBudgeting.heroSubtitle: Envelope budgeting: the method that tells you exactly where your money goes. WonderMoney gives every euro a job before the month begins.
featureBudgeting.whatBody: Envelope budgeting (also called zero-based budgeting) means allocating your entire income to categories before the month starts, until every euro is assigned. When a category runs out, you stop spending there, or consciously move money from another envelope. It is the most effective budgeting method because it forces intentional decisions about every euro.
featureBudgeting.step1Body: Allocate your income across categories: rent, groceries, transport, savings, entertainment. Every euro is assigned until the balance is zero.

featureNetWorth.metaDescription: See your complete financial picture in one place. WonderMoney unifies accounts, investments, and debts into a single number — your net worth. Free and open source.
featureNetWorth.heroTitle: Your financial life, in one number
featureNetWorth.heroSubtitle: WonderMoney unifies your accounts, investments, and debts into a single net worth number. See the full picture, watch it grow, and plan with confidence.
featureNetWorth.step1Body: Link your bank accounts, investment portfolios, and loans via read-only Open Banking. WonderMoney reads your balances without storing credentials.
featureNetWorth.step2Body: Assets minus liabilities, as it changes. WonderMoney shows your net worth in a single, calm number — no spreadsheets, no math.
featureNetWorth.step3Body: A 6-month history chart tracks how your net worth evolves. Trends in, trends out, with no surprises.
featureNetWorth.benefitsTitle: What you can do with WonderMoney net worth
featureNetWorth.benefit1: One number for your entire financial life
featureNetWorth.benefit2: Assets and liabilities, in one view
featureNetWorth.benefit4: Calm by design — we do not move money or sell products
featureNetWorth.faq1Q: What does "net worth" mean in WonderMoney?
featureNetWorth.faq1A: Your net worth is the total of all your assets (bank accounts, investments) minus your liabilities (loans, credit cards). WonderMoney calculates it automatically from your connected accounts.
featureNetWorth.faq2Q: How often does my net worth update?
featureNetWorth.faq2A: WonderMoney refreshes net worth when your connected accounts update — typically once a day for bank balances, and more frequently for investment portfolios. The history chart uses monthly snapshots.
featureNetWorth.faq3Q: Can I exclude accounts from my net worth?
featureNetWorth.faq3A: Yes. Each account, portfolio, and loan can be individually toggled to include or exclude it from your net worth. The dashboard shows the total with the exclusion applied.
featureNetWorth.ctaBody: WonderMoney is free and open source. Use it at wonder.money or run your own.
featureNetWorth.schemaDescription: See your complete financial picture in one place. WonderMoney unifies accounts, investments, and debts into a single net worth number. Free and open source.

featureFinancialMarkets.benefit3: Build a watchlist that follows you

featureFinancialMarkets.faq3A: WonderMoney shows current prices during US market hours and end-of-day snapshots outside market hours. Watchlists update as new prices arrive.

personalFinanceApp.heroSubtitle: WonderMoney connects your bank accounts, tracks your net worth, budgets your spending, and follows your investments — all in one app, built for Europe.
personalFinanceApp.metaTitle: Personal Finance App for Europe — WonderMoney
personalFinanceApp.metaDescription: WonderMoney is a personal finance app that connects to your bank via Open Banking, tracks net worth and investments, and budgets your spending — in one place, for households across Europe.
personalFinanceApp.featuresTitle: Everything Your Money Needs, in One App
personalFinanceApp.feature1Title: All your accounts in one place
personalFinanceApp.feature1Body: Connect current accounts, savings, credit cards, and loans via Open Banking. Balances and transactions sync automatically — no manual entry, no CSV downloads.
personalFinanceApp.feature2Body: See your connected financial data together in one place. Bank data updates when providers supply it, and market values update regularly as available.
personalFinanceApp.feature3Title: Budgeting that keeps up with you
personalFinanceApp.feature3Body: Set monthly budgets by category, and let transactions import and categorise automatically. Always know what's left to spend before the month ends.
personalFinanceApp.feature4Body: Track your portfolio next to your bank accounts, so your complete financial picture — spending, saving, and investing — lives in one dashboard.
personalFinanceApp.feature5Body: Multi-currency support (EUR, GBP, USD and 8 more), so accounts and investments in different currencies still roll up into one clear total.
personalFinanceApp.feature6Body: Invite a partner to share accounts, budgets, and goals in one household — perfect for couples managing money together.
personalFinanceApp.how1Body: Link your bank accounts securely via Open Banking (PSD2). WonderMoney reads balances and transactions — it can never move your money.
personalFinanceApp.how2Body: Transactions sync and categorise automatically. Your budgets, net worth, and investments update as new data arrives.
personalFinanceApp.how3Body: One dashboard for spending, saving, and investing — so you always know where you stand, without opening five different apps.
personalFinanceApp.faq1Q: What makes WonderMoney different from other personal finance apps?
personalFinanceApp.faq1A: Most personal finance apps only do one thing — budgeting, or net worth, or investment tracking. WonderMoney combines Open Banking account sync, envelope budgeting, net worth tracking, and portfolio tracking in a single app, priced for everyday use.
personalFinanceApp.faq2A: Yes. WonderMoney is free to use at wonder.money, or you can run it on your own server.
personalFinanceApp.faq3A: WonderMoney connects to most banks across Europe via Enable Banking, with coverage continuously expanding.
personalFinanceApp.faq4Q: Can my partner and I share an account?

personalFinanceApp.ctaHeadline: Bring Your Whole Financial Life Into One App
personalFinanceApp.ctaBody: Connect your accounts and start tracking your budget, net worth, and investments today. Free and open source.

openBankingApp.heroTitle: The Open Banking App That Brings Every Account Together
openBankingApp.heroSubtitle: WonderMoney connects to your bank accounts via Open Banking (PSD2) — securely, read-only, and automatically. See balances, transactions, budgets, and net worth update without lifting a finger.
openBankingApp.metaTitle: Open Banking App for Europe — WonderMoney
openBankingApp.metaDescription: WonderMoney is an Open Banking app that connects your bank accounts securely via PSD2. Read-only access, automatic transaction sync, and one dashboard for your whole financial life.
openBankingApp.featuresTitle: What Open Banking Unlocks in WonderMoney
openBankingApp.feature1Body: Bank connections use read-only Open Banking through Enable Banking. WonderMoney cannot initiate transfers. You enter your credentials with your bank or provider, and WonderMoney does not see them.
openBankingApp.feature2Body: Transactions sync daily via Open Banking — no manual entry, no CSV downloads, no forgotten spreadsheets.
openBankingApp.feature3Body: WonderMoney connects to most banks across Portugal, Spain, the UK, Germany, France, and other European countries via Enable Banking. Coverage is continuously expanding.
openBankingApp.feature4Body: Current accounts, savings, credit cards, and loans — connect them all through Open Banking and see every balance in one place.
openBankingApp.feature5Body: Your login stays at your bank. You authenticate directly on your bank's portal, and your password never passes through WonderMoney.
openBankingApp.feature6Body: Revoke access to any bank connection whenever you choose, from WonderMoney or directly from your bank's app.
openBankingApp.howTitle: How Open Banking Works in WonderMoney
openBankingApp.how1Body: Search for your bank in WonderMoney and start the connection — no downloads, no paperwork.
openBankingApp.how2Body: You log in on your own bank's secure portal, not inside WonderMoney. Your bank confirms the connection directly with you.
openBankingApp.how3Body: Balances and transactions sync via Open Banking and populate your budgets, net worth, and reports without any manual work.
openBankingApp.faq1A: Open Banking is a European regulation (PSD2) that lets banks securely share account data with authorised providers, at your request. It replaces manual statement downloads with a secure, direct connection.
openBankingApp.faq2Q: Can WonderMoney move money out of my account?
openBankingApp.faq2A: No. Open Banking connections in WonderMoney are strictly read-only. WonderMoney can see your balance and transactions, but it can never initiate a payment or move money.
openBankingApp.faq3Q: Who is WonderMoney's Open Banking provider?
openBankingApp.faq3A: WonderMoney uses Enable Banking, a Registered Account Information Service Provider regulated by Finland's Financial Supervisory Authority (FIN-FSA) and one of Europe's established Open Banking infrastructure providers.
openBankingApp.faq4Q: What happens if I disconnect my bank?
openBankingApp.faq4A: You can revoke access at any time, from WonderMoney or directly from your bank's app. Historical data already synced stays in your account unless you delete it.
openBankingApp.ctaHeadline: Connect Your Bank Accounts the Secure Way
openBankingApp.ctaBody: Link your accounts via Open Banking and let WonderMoney keep your financial picture up to date automatically. Free and open source.

budgetApp.heroTitle: The Budget App That Updates Itself
budgetApp.heroSubtitle: WonderMoney connects to your bank via Open Banking, imports and categorises your transactions automatically, and shows you exactly what's left in every budget category — no manual entry required.
budgetApp.metaDescription: WonderMoney is a budget app that connects to your European bank accounts via Open Banking, automatically categorises transactions, and helps you budget by category — solo or with a partner.
budgetApp.feature1Body: Set a monthly budget for rent, groceries, transport, and more. WonderMoney matches incoming transactions to the right category automatically.
budgetApp.feature2Body: Your bank transactions sync daily via Open Banking. WonderMoney categorises them automatically and deducts from the right budget.
budgetApp.feature3Body: Every category shows how much you've spent and how much is left, so overspending shows up before the month is over, not after.
budgetApp.feature4Body: Compare what you planned to spend against what you actually spent, category by category, and adjust next month accordingly.
budgetApp.feature5Body: Multi-currency support (EUR, GBP, USD and 8 more), so budgets work whether your accounts are in one currency or several.
budgetApp.feature6Body: Household mode lets two people share budgets and categories, so couples can plan spending together instead of guessing.
budgetApp.how1Body: Create budget categories for the things you spend on — rent, groceries, transport, subscriptions — and set a monthly amount for each.
budgetApp.how2Body: Link your accounts via Open Banking. Transactions sync automatically and match to the right budget category.
budgetApp.how3Title: Review and adjust as you go
budgetApp.how3Body: Check your budgets anytime to see what's on track and what's overspent, and move money between categories when plans change.
budgetApp.faq1Q: Do I have to enter transactions manually?
budgetApp.faq1A: No. WonderMoney connects to your bank via Open Banking and imports transactions automatically, matching each one to a budget category.
budgetApp.faq2Q: What budgeting method does WonderMoney use?
budgetApp.faq2A: WonderMoney supports category-based budgeting: you allocate a monthly amount to each category, and spending is tracked against it automatically as transactions arrive.
budgetApp.faq3Q: Can I budget with my partner?
budgetApp.faq3A: Yes. Household mode lets two people share budgets, categories, and accounts in one place, with billing managed by a single plan.
budgetApp.faq4A: Yes. WonderMoney is free to use at wonder.money, or you can run it on your own server.
budgetApp.ctaHeadline: Start Budgeting Without the Manual Work
budgetApp.ctaBody: Connect your bank accounts and let WonderMoney track your budget automatically. Free and open source.

adNetWorth.metaTitle: Do You Know What You're Worth? — WonderMoney
adNetWorth.metaDescription: See your complete net worth in one place — bank accounts, investments, and debts combined automatically. Free and open source.
adNetWorth.heroTitle: Do you actually know what you're worth?
adNetWorth.heroSubtitle: Most people can tell you their salary to the euro. Almost nobody can tell you their real net worth. WonderMoney connects your accounts and investments to show you the number that actually matters.
adNetWorth.painTitle: Why most people have no idea
adNetWorth.pain1Body: A current account here, a savings account there, an investment platform somewhere else. Nobody adds it all up — so nobody knows the real total.
adNetWorth.pain2Body: Even if you built a net worth spreadsheet once, updating it by hand every month is the first habit to slip.
adNetWorth.pain3Body: Net worth isn't just what you own — it's what you own minus what you owe. Most people only track one side of that equation.
adNetWorth.how1Body: Link your bank accounts and investment platforms via secure, read-only Open Banking.
adNetWorth.how2Body: Balances, portfolio value, and debts combine into one net worth figure that updates as your providers supply new data.
adNetWorth.how3Body: See your net worth trend month by month, so you know if you're actually moving in the right direction.
adNetWorth.ctaHeadline: Find out what you're actually worth
adNetWorth.ctaBody: Connect your accounts and see your real net worth — automatically, in one place.

adFragmentation.metaTitle: One App Instead of Five — WonderMoney
adFragmentation.metaDescription: Stop juggling bank apps, broker apps, and spreadsheets. See every account in one place with WonderMoney. Free and open source.
adFragmentation.heroTitle: 5 bank apps. 2 broker apps. 1 spreadsheet. There's a better way.
adFragmentation.heroSubtitle: You shouldn't need six logins to answer one question: how am I doing financially? WonderMoney brings every account into a single view.
adFragmentation.painTitle: Juggling apps costs you more than time
adFragmentation.pain1Title: You check five apps and still don't know the answer
adFragmentation.pain1Body: Each app shows one slice of your finances. None of them shows the whole picture — so the real question stays unanswered.
adFragmentation.pain2Title: The spreadsheet is always out of date
adFragmentation.pain2Body: You built it once to tie everything together. Updating it by hand every month is the part that never survives.
adFragmentation.pain3Body: When your accounts live in five different places, it's easy for a subscription or fee to slip past you unseen.
adFragmentation.how1Body: Link your bank accounts and investment platforms via secure, read-only Open Banking — no more switching apps.
adFragmentation.how2Body: Balances, spending, and investments sit side by side, automatically categorized and kept in sync.
adFragmentation.how3Body: Open WonderMoney and get the full picture — no more app-hopping to piece it together.
adFragmentation.ctaBody: Connect every account and see your whole financial picture in a single place.

adOpenBanking.metaTitle: Your Bank Has to Share Your Data If You Ask — WonderMoney
adOpenBanking.metaDescription: EU law requires your bank to share your data with apps you authorize. WonderMoney uses this to show your full financial picture automatically. Free and open source.
adOpenBanking.heroTitle: Your bank is legally required to share your data with apps you authorize. Most people don't know this.
adOpenBanking.heroSubtitle: Open Banking (PSD2) gives you the right to connect your accounts to apps like WonderMoney — securely, and only with your permission. It turns five separate logins into one clear picture.
adOpenBanking.painTitle: The right most people never use
adOpenBanking.pain1Title: It's not a workaround — it's the law
adOpenBanking.pain1Body: Under PSD2, EU banks must let you share your account data with authorized apps, on your terms.
adOpenBanking.pain2Title: Your bank still holds your money
adOpenBanking.pain2Body: Open Banking is read-only. WonderMoney can see your data to show it to you — it can't move money or make payments.
adOpenBanking.pain3Body: You choose which accounts to connect, and you can disconnect at any time from your bank or from WonderMoney.
adOpenBanking.how1Body: Pick your bank and confirm the connection directly with them — WonderMoney never sees your banking credentials.
adOpenBanking.how2Body: Your bank shares balances and transactions with WonderMoney under the permission you granted. Nothing more.
adOpenBanking.how3Title: See it all in one place
adOpenBanking.how3Body: Every connected account feeds into a single dashboard — balances, spending, and net worth, kept in sync.
adOpenBanking.ctaHeadline: Put your legal right to work
adOpenBanking.ctaBody: Connect your accounts and see your full financial picture — securely, on your terms.

featureHousehold.metaTitle: Shared household finances with private accounts | WonderMoney
featureHousehold.metaDescription: Manage money with your partner or family: everyone signs in with their own login, shares the accounts they choose and keeps the rest private. Split costs with friends in groups.
featureHousehold.heroTitle: Manage money together, keep what's yours private
featureHousehold.heroSubtitle: Invite the people you live with to one household. Each signs in with their own login, shares the accounts they choose and sees the household's numbers in their own currency.
featureHousehold.schemaDescription: Shared household finances with a login for each person, four roles, private accounts, a filter by member, ownership shares and shared expense groups.
featureHousehold.whatTitle: One household, everyone with their own login
featureHousehold.whatBody: A household holds the accounts, budgets, goals and net worth you manage together. Up to six people can be in it, each with their own login and a role that decides what they can change.
featureHousehold.whatPoint1Body: Owner, admin, member or viewer. A viewer sees the shared data but can't change it.
featureHousehold.whatPoint2Body: Keep an account to yourself, or let each person view it or edit it. Nobody else sees it, the household's owner included.
featureHousehold.whatPoint3Body: Mark joint accounts, say who spent a transaction, and filter transactions, reports, budgets and net worth by person.
featureHousehold.whatPoint4Body: Split an account by percentage, such as a house fund held 60/40, and each person's net worth counts their part.
featureHousehold.step1Body: Your household is created with your account, and you are its owner. You can hand ownership to someone else later.
featureHousehold.step2Body: Pick each person's role. The link works only for the address you invited, and expires after seven days.
featureHousehold.step3Body: Accounts are shared with the household by default. Make one private and choose, for each person, hidden, view or edit.
featureHousehold.groupsTitle: Split costs with friends, flatmates and trips
featureHousehold.groupsBody: A group is a set of people who share costs. Share a transaction with it and WonderMoney splits it, works out who owes whom, and counts only your household's share in your spending.
featureHousehold.groupsPoint1: Add people by name: they don't need a WonderMoney account
featureHousehold.groupsPoint2: Split equally, by amount or by percentage
featureHousehold.groupsPoint3: A balance for each person, and the fewest payments to settle up
featureHousehold.groupsPoint4: Record a settlement and link it to the transfer that paid it
featureHousehold.faq1Q: Can the household's owner see my private accounts?
featureHousehold.faq1A: No. A private account is visible only to you and to the people you share it with. The owner and admins don't see it unless you share it with them.
featureHousehold.faq2Q: How many people can be in a household?
featureHousehold.faq2A: Up to six, the owner included. On your own server, you can change that number.
featureHousehold.faq3A: Their private accounts stay in the household, shared as they were: the people who had access keep it, and nobody else gains it. The money they spent counts as Shared.
featureHousehold.ctaHeadline: Bring the household into one place
featureHousehold.ctaBody: Invite the people you live with and choose what each account shares.

featureImports.metaTitle: Import bank statements: CSV, Excel, OFX, QIF and CAMT.053 | WonderMoney
featureImports.metaDescription: Import transactions from any bank's CSV, Excel, OFX, QIF or CAMT.053 export, or move your history from YNAB or Actual Budget. Review every row before anything is added.
featureImports.heroTitle: Bring in any statement, and nothing twice
featureImports.heroSubtitle: When a bank can't be connected, or you want the history from before it was, import the file your bank gives you. You check every row before anything is added.
featureImports.schemaDescription: Import bank statements from CSV, Excel, OFX, QFX, QIF and CAMT.053 files, and transaction history from YNAB and Actual Budget, with a review step and duplicate detection.
featureImports.whatTitle: Every file your bank gives you
featureImports.whatBody: Download the statement and leave it as the bank wrote it. WonderMoney finds the date, description and amount columns and works out the date and number formats, so it reads most banks' exports without a template.
featureImports.whatPoint1: CSV with any delimiter, and Excel (.xls, .xlsx)
featureImports.whatPoint2: OFX, QFX and QIF, from banks, Quicken, Microsoft Money and GnuCash
featureImports.whatPoint3: CAMT.053, the ISO 20022 statement of SEPA banks
featureImports.whatPoint4: Files with several accounts, each sent to one of yours
featureImports.whatPoint5: Your YNAB register, with its accounts and categories matched to yours
featureImports.whatPoint6: Actual Budget's transactions export, with transfers kept as transfers
featureImports.step1Body: Open the account and choose Import transactions. WonderMoney reads the file and shows how many transactions it found and the dates they cover.
featureImports.step2Body: Each row is new, already in the account, a possible duplicate, or couldn't be read. Tick or untick any of them.
featureImports.step3Body: The import runs in the background. If it stops part way, try again: it carries on where it stopped and imports nothing twice.
featureImports.reviewTitle: Nothing is added until you check it
featureImports.reviewBody: The same purchase often arrives twice, once from bank sync and once from a file. The review shows every row and what will happen to it, so you decide.
featureImports.reviewPoint1Body: A row with the same amount as a transaction already in the account, up to three days apart, is skipped unless you include it.
featureImports.reviewPoint2Body: Rows that are already in the account are skipped, so importing an overlapping export adds only what is new.
featureImports.reviewPoint3Body: Imported rows are categorised the same way as the transactions bank sync brings in, and the household's rules apply to them.
featureImports.faq1Q: Which banks does it work with?
featureImports.faq1A: Any bank that exports a statement as CSV, Excel, OFX, QIF or CAMT.053. For Millennium BCP, ActivoBank, Bankinter, Banco BPI and Montepio, WonderMoney also reads the bank's own format.
featureImports.faq2Q: Can I import on my phone?
featureImports.faq2A: Yes, CSV, OFX, QIF and CAMT.053 files, with the same review before anything is imported. YNAB and Actual Budget exports are imported on the web.
featureImports.faq3Q: Can I move from YNAB or Actual Budget?
featureImports.faq3A: Yes, with your transaction history: each account and category is matched to one of yours, and transfers stay linked. Budget amounts and goals are not imported.
featureImports.ctaBody: Import the statements you already have and start from the full picture.

featureRecurring.metaTitle: Track bills, subscriptions and recurring payments | WonderMoney
featureRecurring.metaDescription: WonderMoney finds the payments that repeat, from rent to subscriptions, shows them on a calendar, projects each account's balance for the next 30 days and can put your bills in your own calendar app.
featureRecurring.heroTitle: See what's coming before it leaves your account
featureRecurring.heroSubtitle: WonderMoney spots rent, salary, subscriptions and the other payments that repeat, so you know what is paid, what is due and where your balance is heading.
featureRecurring.schemaDescription: Recurring payment detection with a bills calendar, a 30-day balance forecast for each account and an iCal feed of upcoming bills.
featureRecurring.whatTitle: Your bills and subscriptions, found for you
featureRecurring.whatBody: Detection runs whenever transactions are added, imported or synced. The payments it is sure of are listed at once; the others wait for you to confirm them.
featureRecurring.whatPoint1: Repeating payments and income found in your transactions
featureRecurring.whatPoint2: Confirm or dismiss each one, and restore it later
featureRecurring.whatPoint3: A calendar that marks each bill paid, due, overdue or projected
featureRecurring.whatPoint4: A 30-day balance forecast on each account, with its lowest point
featureRecurring.step1Body: From bank sync, a file import or by hand. WonderMoney looks for the payments that repeat.
featureRecurring.step2Body: Check each payment's merchant, usual amount and frequency, then confirm it or mark it as not recurring.
featureRecurring.step3Body: Read the month on the calendar and each account's forecast. A bill already paid drops out of the forecast, so it never counts twice.
featureRecurring.calendarTitle: Your bills in the calendar you already use
featureRecurring.calendarBody: Publish your confirmed bills as a read-only calendar feed, and subscribe to it once in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or any app that reads iCal.
featureRecurring.calendarPoint1: An all-day event for each bill in the next 90 days
featureRecurring.calendarPoint2: The bill's name and expected amount, in your language
featureRecurring.calendarPoint3: No balances, account names or account numbers
featureRecurring.calendarPoint4: Reset or revoke the link whenever you want
featureRecurring.faq1Q: Do projected payments count in my reports?
featureRecurring.faq1A: No. A projection is not a transaction: it stays out of reports, budgets and totals until the payment is recorded.
featureRecurring.faq2Q: Does it need a bank connection?
featureRecurring.faq2A: No. Detection runs on every transaction that is added, whether it came from bank sync, a file or your own entry.
featureRecurring.faq3Q: Who sees the bills of a private account?
featureRecurring.faq3A: Only the people who can see that account. Recurring payments, forecasts and the calendar feed follow the account's sharing.
featureRecurring.ctaHeadline: Know what's due before it's due
featureRecurring.ctaBody: Let WonderMoney find your recurring payments and plan the month around them.

featureAssistant.metaTitle: AI assistant for your personal finances | WonderMoney
featureAssistant.metaDescription: Ask about your spending, budgets, goals and portfolio in plain words. The assistant reads your data, proposes changes for you to apply and stays off until you turn it on. Connect Claude Desktop or Cursor over MCP.
featureAssistant.heroSubtitle: How much went on restaurants this month? Which budget is running over? The assistant answers from your own accounts, and changes nothing without you.
featureAssistant.schemaDescription: An AI assistant that answers questions about your accounts, spending, budgets, goals and portfolio, proposes changes for you to confirm, and a read-only MCP server for AI clients.
featureAssistant.whatTitle: An assistant that reads, and asks before it changes
featureAssistant.whatBody: The assistant answers questions about your accounts, spending, budgets, goals and portfolio. It can draft a change, such as a category for a set of transactions, but nothing happens until you apply it.
featureAssistant.whatPoint1: Answers from your own data, under the same sharing rules as the app
featureAssistant.whatPoint2: Off until you turn it on, and you can turn it off again in settings
featureAssistant.whatPoint3: Proposes categories, reviewed marks and notes for you to apply or dismiss
featureAssistant.whatPoint4: One switch hides every AI feature, and the server refuses them too
featureAssistant.step1Body: The assistant stays off until you choose Enable assistant on its consent screen in the web app.
featureAssistant.step2Body: Ask about a month, a category, a budget or a goal. It reads the data you can see in the app, and nothing more.
featureAssistant.step3Body: A proposed change shows each transaction's current value and the proposed one. Apply it, dismiss it, or let it expire after seven days.
featureAssistant.mcpBody: WonderMoney runs a read-only MCP server. Connect Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or another MCP client with a token, and ask about your finances from its chat.
featureAssistant.mcpPoint1: Read-only tools for balances, spending, budgets, goals and portfolio
featureAssistant.mcpPoint2: The client sees exactly what you see, and never another household's data
featureAssistant.mcpPoint3: Optional proposals that wait for you to apply them in the app
featureAssistant.mcpPoint4: Its own token, which expires after 90 days and can be revoked
featureAssistant.faq1A: No. It can't move money, start transactions or change bank records. It reads your data and can only propose changes that you apply yourself.
featureAssistant.faq2A: No. It stays off until you turn it on. To turn off every AI feature at once, use Hide AI features in Settings › Privacy.
featureAssistant.faq3Q: Does it see the private accounts of others in my household?
featureAssistant.faq3A: Only the ones shared with you. A private account hidden from you stays hidden from the assistant and from MCP clients too, and your proposals are visible only to you.
featureAssistant.ctaBody: Turn the assistant on when you want it, and keep every change in your hands.

featureMultiCurrency.metaDescription: Keep accounts in euros, dollars, pounds or any other currency and see every total in yours, converted at the European Central Bank's daily rates. An amount without a rate is flagged, not guessed.
featureMultiCurrency.heroSubtitle: Accounts and transactions can be in any currency. WonderMoney shows every total in yours, and says plainly when an amount couldn't be converted.
featureMultiCurrency.schemaDescription: Accounts and transactions in any currency, with totals converted at the European Central Bank's daily reference rates and amounts without a rate flagged.
featureMultiCurrency.whatTitle: Converted at the rate of each day
featureMultiCurrency.whatBody: Every amount in another currency is converted at the European Central Bank's rate for its date, which covers the main currencies. Rates update on working days, with nothing to set up.
featureMultiCurrency.whatPoint1: Accounts and transactions in any currency
featureMultiCurrency.whatPoint2: Totals in your currency at the ECB's daily reference rates
featureMultiCurrency.whatPoint3: The original amount shown under the converted one
featureMultiCurrency.whatPoint4: An amount with no rate marked Not converted and left out of totals
featureMultiCurrency.whatPoint5: Marked Estimated when the only rate is more than a week old, and converted again when a newer one comes
featureMultiCurrency.step1Title: Add accounts in their own currency
featureMultiCurrency.step1Body: A current account in euros, a brokerage account in dollars, savings in pounds: each keeps its currency.
featureMultiCurrency.step2Body: Net worth, cash flow, reports and totals are shown in it.
featureMultiCurrency.step3Body: When a total leaves an amount out, it says how many and in which currencies, so it never adds two currencies together.
featureMultiCurrency.householdTitle: Each person in their own currency
featureMultiCurrency.householdBody: In a household, everyone picks their own currency and sees every total in it. The other members' balances and transactions are converted before they are added.
featureMultiCurrency.householdPoint1: Net worth, cash flow and spending in each member's currency
featureMultiCurrency.householdPoint2: Budgets keep the currency they were created in
featureMultiCurrency.householdPoint3: Portfolio history converted at the rate of each day
featureMultiCurrency.householdPoint4: Balances in shared expense groups kept per currency, never converted
featureMultiCurrency.faq1A: Accounts and transactions can be in any currency. Conversion uses the European Central Bank's reference rates, which cover the main currencies; an amount in a currency without a rate stays in its own currency and out of your totals.
featureMultiCurrency.faq2Q: Do I need to enter exchange rates?
featureMultiCurrency.faq2A: No. Rates are fetched automatically on working days, and estimated or unconverted amounts are converted again after each update.
featureMultiCurrency.faq3Q: Why does a total say it is incomplete?
featureMultiCurrency.faq3A: Because an amount in it had no exchange rate. WonderMoney leaves it out rather than add it at face value, and tells you which currencies were missing.
featureMultiCurrency.ctaHeadline: See all your money in one currency
featureMultiCurrency.ctaBody: Add accounts in any currency and read one total you can trust.

featureSelfHosting.metaTitle: Self-hosted personal finance app with an API | WonderMoney
featureSelfHosting.metaDescription: WonderMoney is open source under the AGPL. Run it on your own server with one Docker Compose file, sign in with your own identity provider and connect scripts through the REST API.
featureSelfHosting.heroTitle: Run it on your own server
featureSelfHosting.heroSubtitle: WonderMoney is free and open source. Use it at wonder.money, or run the same app on a home server, a NAS or a small VPS, with your data in your own database.
featureSelfHosting.schemaDescription: Open-source personal finance software under the AGPL that runs on your own server with Docker Compose or Kubernetes, with single sign-on and a REST API with personal tokens.
featureSelfHosting.whatTitle: The same app, on your machine
featureSelfHosting.whatBody: A self-hosted server has the same app as wonder.money: accounts, bank sync, budgets, goals, loans, households and portfolios. The optional extras switch on when you configure them, and stay hidden when you don't.
featureSelfHosting.whatPoint1: One Docker Compose file runs Postgres, the API, a background worker and the web app
featureSelfHosting.whatPoint2: About 2 GB of free memory: a small VPS, a home server or a NAS
featureSelfHosting.whatPoint3: AI features with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a local Ollama included
featureSelfHosting.whatPoint4: Single sign-on with your own identity provider, such as Authentik or Keycloak
featureSelfHosting.whatPoint5: Bank sync with your own Enable Banking key, and SimpleFIN for US and Canadian banks
featureSelfHosting.step1Body: Docker with the Compose plugin and about 2 GB of free memory is enough.
featureSelfHosting.step2Body: The install script sets up the containers and generates the secrets. Add a domain and HTTPS to use it outside your own network.
featureSelfHosting.step3Body: Create your account, or restore an export from wonder.money: an export loads into an empty household on another server.
featureSelfHosting.apiTitle: An API for your own scripts
featureSelfHosting.apiBody: Give a script, a spreadsheet or a home dashboard access to your finances with a personal API token, on wonder.money or on your own server.
featureSelfHosting.apiPoint1: A REST API with a public reference
featureSelfHosting.apiPoint2: Read or write access, which never reaches deletes, bank connections or the household
featureSelfHosting.apiPoint3: Tokens that expire after 30, 90 or 365 days
featureSelfHosting.apiPoint4: Only a hash of each token is kept, so it is shown once
featureSelfHosting.faq1A: Yes. The code is open source under the GNU AGPL v3, and the hosted service at wonder.money is free too.
featureSelfHosting.faq2Q: Does bank sync work on my own server?
featureSelfHosting.faq2A: Yes. Nothing is needed on the server: each person adds their own Enable Banking key in Settings. You can also turn on SimpleFIN for banks in the United States and Canada.
featureSelfHosting.faq3Q: Can I move between wonder.money and my own server?
featureSelfHosting.faq3A: Yes. Export your data from one and restore it into an empty household on the other.
featureSelfHosting.ctaBody: Start at wonder.money and move to your own server whenever you want, or the other way round.
